The source frames recent suicide bombings as posing a novel problem for trauma centers, namely the massive simultaneous arrival of many gravely wounded patients, and reports the experience of a Level 2 Trauma Center in Afghanistan during the February 2007 wave of suicide bombings, during which 14 casualties were received.
Triage in that series occurred in two stages: a first triage by the U.S.

Army Level I group prior to evacuation, and a second surgical triage carried out with a systematic ultrasound examination, after which four cases with ISS greater than 25 were re-categorized and underwent emergency surgical procedures.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Definition or description of 'The Main Gate Syndrome' as a clinical entity/format.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Explicit designation as a 'new format' (and the 'Main Gate Syndrome' label) for mass-casualty victim surge management.

Tacrolimus concentrations measured by the affinity column-mediated immunoassay (ACMIA) method in 154 samples from kidney or liver transplant recipients closely correlated with those measured by the microparticle enzyme immunoassay (MEIA) method (r = 0.84), supporting the comparability of the two assays.
The Bland-Altman plot using concentration differences between the 2 methods and the average of the 2 methods showed no specific trends.

The tacrolimus levels determined by both the MEIA method and the ACMIA method were not influenced by hematocrit levels, but the difference between the 2 methods (ACMIA - MEIA) tended to be larger in low hematocrit samples (P<.001).

A case report describes cerebro-mediastinal tuberculosis in an immuno-competent child, a seven-year-old girl, an occurrence the authors state had not been previously described, and the child described also had a probable Say-Barber-Miller syndrome.

The child presented with infantile encephalopathy since birth characterized by facial dysmorphy evocative of a bird face, microcephaly and mental retardation, together with recurrent infections and several months of back pain with anorexia and weight loss.

Spinal and cerebral MRI showed a mediastinal mass involving the spine and cerebral lesions evocative of tuberculomas, the tuberculin interdermal reaction was positive, and culture of a vertebral biopsy was positive for Koch bacillus.
Anti-tuberculosis treatment improved the child's general and local status.

No established causative link is reported between probable Say-Barber-Miller syndrome and cerebromediastinal tuberculosis; the report only discusses a putative causative link between the syndrome and the occurrence of tuberculosis, and notes that an extensive immunological work-up was normal.

Because the evidence is a single descriptive case report, the proposed association between the probable Say-Barber-Miller syndrome and the occurrence of tuberculosis cannot by itself establish causation.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: an established causal relationship between probable Say-Barber-Miller syndrome and cerebromediastinal tuberculosis.

No — in a cross-sectional study using a prospective database of all consecutive endoscopies over 15 years in which colorectal cancer was diagnosed, colorectal cancer was diagnosed in 835 patients, and assuming that these cancers developed from an adenoma, only 11 out of 835 (1.3%) cancers were missed in the adenoma phase; 25 of these patients had undergone a previous endoscopy without a cancer diagnosis, five of those 25 underwent regular surveillance, and only 11 patients had no argument for regular follow-up.

Yes, in a swine extremity arterial injury model, direct application of the zeolite mineral QuikClot Advanced Clotting Sponge (QC-ACS) over the lacerated femoral artery decreased total blood loss compared with a control group given a pressure dressing with manual pressure over a gauze sponge.

In the same study of 16 swine (control n=6, QC n=10) with a 5 mm femoral artery incision, QC application led to a slower drop in blood pressure, while the control group had a significantly higher increase in lactate within 60 minutes and a significantly increased mean prothrombin time at 60 minutes; the QC group had significantly higher hematocrit levels.

The cited evidence is mixed: in a retrospective series of 145 patients with gallbladder polyps, neoplastic polyps were more frequently found in patients with a rapid growth rate greater than 0.6 mm/mo, but on multivariate analysis the growth rate was not related to the neoplastic nature of a polyp.

In that study, the growth rate was determined from the change in size per time interval between 2 ultrasonographic examinations (mm/mo), and the 145 patients with gallbladder polyps were retrospectively investigated at Samsung Medical Center, South Korea, from 1994 to 2007, having undergone at least 1 ultrasonographic follow-up examination over an interval greater than 6 months before cholecystectomy.

On multivariate analysis, older age (>60 y) and large polyp size (>10 mm) were significantly associated with neoplastic polyps, whereas the growth rate was not, and neoplastic polyps were also more frequently found in patients with hypertension and in those with a polyp size greater than 10 mm.

The cited evidence is mixed rather than a clear yes or no: in a retrospective national sample of veterans with ischemic stroke, overall performance was above 70% for 10 of the 14 inpatient quality indicators examined, yet older patients were less likely than younger patients to receive several specific processes of care.

Inpatient stroke care quality was assessed across 14 processes of care: dysphagia screening, NIHSS score documentation, thrombolysis, deep venous thrombosis prophylaxis, antithrombotic therapy by hospital day 2 and at discharge, early ambulation, fall risk assessment, pressure ulcer risk assessment, rehabilitation needs assessment, atrial fibrillation management, lipid management, smoking cessation counseling, and stroke education.

The study was a retrospective national sample of veterans admitted to 129 Veterans Affairs medical centers for ischemic stroke during fiscal year 2007, comprising 3,939 veterans whose mean age was 67.8 years (standard deviation, 11.5).

In unadjusted analyses, older patients were less likely than younger patients to receive lipid management, smoking cessation, NIHSS documentation, and early ambulation, while older patients were more likely to receive dysphagia screening and stroke education.

After adjustment for demographic, clinical, and hospital-level characteristics, age-related differences in processes of care were less consistent, although the youngest patients were more likely to receive smoking cessation counseling and the oldest patients were less likely to receive lipid management.

Because the evidence comes from a retrospective study of inpatient process measures among veterans with ischemic stroke treated in Veterans Affairs medical centers, it cannot establish whether stroke care is adequate for older patients across all settings, care processes, and clinical outcomes; this is a limitation entailed by the study design, not a reported outcome.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: overall adequacy of stroke care across all settings, care processes, and clinical outcomes.

The cited evidence is mixed on whether MRI accurately predicts concordant pain provocation during provocative disc injection: in 62 patients (aged 17-68 years) with axial low back pain likely to be disc related who underwent lumbar discography (178 discs tested), the combination of disc protrusion with a high intensity zone correlated significantly with concordant pain provocation (P<0.01), with sensitivity 45.5%, specificity 97.8% and positive predictive value 87.0%, indicating high specificity but low sensitivity.
A normal or bulging disc with a high intensity zone was not associated with reproduction of pain on provocation discography.

In the same study, disc degeneration (sensitivity 95.4%; specificity 38.8%; PPV 33.9%), disc protrusion (sensitivity 68.2%; specificity 80.6%; PPV 53.6%), and high intensity zone alone (sensitivity 56.8%; specificity 83.6%; PPV 53.2%) were not helpful in identifying a disc with concordant pain.

In a human cadaver biomechanical study of sternal closure, midline sternotomy was performed in 18 human cadavers, and four sternal closure techniques were tested: (1) approximation with six interrupted steel wires; (2) approximation with six interrupted cables; (3) closure 1 (wires) or 2 (cables) reinforced with a transverse sternal plate at the sixth rib; (4) closure using 4 sternal plates alone; the study tested the hypothesis that sternal closure stability can be improved by adding plate fixation in this human cadaver model.

Intrathoracic pressure was increased in all techniques while sternal separation was measured by three pairs of sonomicrometry crystals fixed at the upper, middle and lower parts of the sternum until 2.0 mm separation was detected.

Intrathoracic pressure was increased in all techniques while sternal separation was measured by three pairs of sonomicrometry crystals fixed at the upper, middle and lower parts of the sternum until 2.0 mm separation was detected; the intrathoracic pressure required to cause 2.0 mm separation increased significantly from 183.3 +/- 123.9 to 301.4 +/- 204.5 in wires/cables alone vs. wires/cables plus one plate respectively, and to 355.0 +/- 210.4 in the 4 plates group (p<0.05).

Regression Coefficients (95% CI) were 120 (47-194) and 142 (66-219) respectively for the plate groups, and differences in displacement pressures were analyzed using repeated measures ANOVA and Regression Coefficients.

These results come from a human cadaver biomechanical model with sternal separation measured under applied intrathoracic pressure, so they establish mechanical stability of the closure construct in that model rather than clinical sternal stability in patients.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: effect of sternal plating on secondary sternal closure.

Israeli hospital readiness for terrorism-related multiple casualty incidents rests on a guideline set 15 years earlier by the Emergency and Disaster Medicine Division of the Israeli Ministry of Health, which defined 20 percent of each hospital's bed capacity as its readiness for multiple casualties; half of those casualties are expected to require immediate medical treatment, and an HMCI is defined as 10 or more casualties, or 4 or more with an ISS of 16 or greater, arriving at a single hospital.

The study was performed to evaluate the efficacy of those current readiness guidelines on the basis of the epidemiology of encountered HMCIs, using a retrospective record of HMCIs from the Israeli Defense Force home front command and the Israeli National Trauma Registry between November 2000 and June 2003.

For surge capacity, the study covered 32 attacks that produced 62 HMCIs and 1292 casualties, with a mean of 20.8 +/- 13.3 arriving casualties per single hospital (range 4-56, median 16.5), and in 95% of the HMCIs the casualty load was 52 or fewer.

Because the reported figures are the observed distribution of casualties arriving at single hospitals during HMCIs rather than a validated forecasting tool, they can be compared against the 20 percent-of-bed-capacity readiness key, but the cited evidence does not report a formal model for better predicting surge capacity.

For injury severity distribution, the readiness guideline assumes half of casualties require immediate medical treatment, whereas in the Israeli HMCI data 1022 (79.2%) casualties did not necessitate immediate medical treatment based on severity scores and emergency department discharges.

In a comparison of terror and war trauma hospitalizations among 1784 civilians and 802 soldiers, critical injuries and injuries to multiple body regions were more likely in terror than war, soldiers tended to present with less severe injuries from war than from terror, and in-hospital mortality was higher among terror (7%) than war (2%) casualties, particularly among civilians.

In a cross-sectional study of 96 men aged 40 or more in the South Metropolitan Region of Santiago de Chile who were surveyed with the ADAM questionnaire and sampled for total testosterone, SHBG and albumin, the ADAM tool detected PADAM with 83.3% sensitivity but only 19.7% specificity when available testosterone <198.4 ng/dL was used as the gold standard, indicating high sensitivity but poor specificity as a screening instrument.

PADAM was considered present if items 1 or 7 or any 3 other questions of the ADAM questionnaire were positive; 78 of the 96 men (81.3%) were identified as possible PADAM by the questionnaire, whereas available testosterone confirmed the diagnosis in 27 cases (28.1%) overall.
Item 1 of the ADAM questionnaire (decreased sexual desire) was a better predictor of hypogonadism than the complete questionnaire, with 63.3% sensitivity and 66.7% specificity.

Because the cited evidence comes from a cross-sectional design, it quantifies the agreement between questionnaire responses and the testosterone threshold but cannot establish that screening with the ADAM questionnaire alters clinical outcomes.

In ambulatory children with spina bifida, peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) from graded treadmill testing largely reflected maximum oxygen uptake, but the evidence is mixed: although there were no significant differences between VO2peak and VO2 during a supramaximal protocol (VO2supramaximal), 5 of the 20 children did show improvement during supramaximal testing.

VO2peak was measured during a graded treadmill exercise test, and its validity was evaluated using previously described guidelines for maximum exercise testing in children who are healthy, as well as the difference between VO2peak and VO2 during a supramaximal protocol (VO2supramaximal).

Among the 20 participating children with spina bifida who were ambulatory, 15 met at least 2 of the 3 previously described criteria for maximum exercise testing, and 1 child failed to meet any criteria.

In eight chronic hemodialysis patients, daily oral sodium bicarbonate supplementation for 10-14 days significantly raised blood pH and serum bicarbonate, yet the fractional synthesis rates of muscle protein and of albumin did not change significantly, so increasing blood pH did not stimulate protein synthesis in this population.
Fractional synthesis rates of muscle protein and albumin in that study were obtained with the L-[(2)H(5)ring]phenylalanine flooding technique.
Oral NaHCO(3) supplementation raised serum bicarbonate from 21.5 +/- 3.4 to 28.6 +/- 1.6 mmol/l (p = 0.018) and blood pH from 7.41 to 7.46 (p = 0.041) in these hemodialysis patients.

The muscle protein fractional synthesis rate was 2.1 +/- 0.2% per day before versus 2.0 +/- 0.5% per day after alkalization (p = 0.39), and the albumin fractional synthesis rate was 8.3 +/- 2.2 versus 8.6 +/- 2.5% per day (p = 0.31), neither change being significant.

Determination between complete and incomplete traumatic spinal cord injury is clinically relevant to neurological prognosis: in the MPSS trial, patients with complete motor loss showed an average ASIA motor score improvement of 9.0 points in the MPSS group versus 12.6 points in the non-MPSS group, while patients with incomplete motor loss improved by 14.1 and 15.5 points respectively, so incomplete injuries recovered substantially more points than complete injuries in both treatment groups.

For pressure ulcer risk, the cited evidence is partial: pressure ulcers are described as common complications in patients with complete spinal cord injury or incomplete injury in which sensory function is spared, and a retrospective, cross-sectional study of patients with complete and incomplete injuries (American Spinal Injury Association Grades A and B) covered by the State Welfare Organization of Iran found a pressure ulcer in 39.2% of all patients with spinal cord injury (71.8% of those with traumatic versus 28.2% of those with nontraumatic injury), while sufficient data were unavailable for 94 patients (1.6%); this study did not directly compare pressure ulcer occurrence or severity between complete and incomplete traumatic spinal cord injury.

For acute hospital outcomes, the cited evidence is partial: a retrospective chart review of 193 patients with acute traumatic spinal cord injury hospitalized between 2006 and 2012 used multivariate logistic regression (enter method) to assess the relative contribution of SIRS+ at admission in predicting mortality, intensive care unit length of stay, hospital length of stay, and at least one major complication during acute hospitalization, with American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale grade and patient age included as covariates, but the retrieved evidence does not report the effect estimates or independent association of AIS grade (complete versus incomplete) with those outcomes.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: direct comparison of pressure ulcer occurrence or severity between complete and incomplete traumatic SCI.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: reported effect estimates or independent association of AIS grade with mortality, ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, or major complications.

Opioid dependence and methadone maintenance treatment (MMT) are documented in the medical record, but documentation is frequently missing: among 84 patients from a methadone clinic who received primary care at an affiliated but separate medical center, opioid dependence documentation was absent in 30% (95% CI, 20%-41%) and MMT documentation was absent from either the last primary care note or the last hospital discharge summary in 11% (95% CI, 5%-19%).

Electronic medical records of those patients were reviewed for documentation of methadone, opioid dependence, and potential drug-methadone interactions, and the proportions of records lacking opioid dependence and methadone documentation were then estimated.

The study was designed to identify potential safety risks among MMT patients engaged in medical care by evaluating how often opioid dependence and MMT documentation are missing from medical records and by characterizing potential medication-methadone interactions.

The retrieved evidence does not establish that foreign bodies migrate towards the heart: of 3,000 foreign bodies collected over 40 years, four showed extra-lumen migration, in two the migration started in the esophagus (one reaching the aorta and the other the neck area) and in the other two it started in the pharynx (one moving towards the prevertebral fascia and the other externalizing in the submandibular region), with no case of migration to or towards the heart reported.

The source presents 'foreign bodies walk to the heart' as a popular saying linked to fixation of foreign bodies in the mucosa favouring migration, rather than as a demonstrated route to the heart; it also notes that only four of the 3,000 foreign bodies analysed had extra-lumen migration.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: migration to or towards the heart.

Yes, ESC could change the way people drive: although research indicates ESC reduces collision rates and saves lives, drivers may show behavioral adaptation to or overreliance on ESC that could offset or reduce its overall effectiveness.

In a Canadian telephone survey of 1017 owners/drivers of 2006-2008 ESC-equipped passenger vehicles in Quebec and British Columbia, 23% of ESC owners who knew their vehicle had ESC reported noticing long-lasting changes in their driving behavior since they began driving that vehicle.

Interpretation: these figures come from drivers' self-reported perceptions in telephone surveys, a design that documents reported awareness and perceived behavior change rather than measured driving behavior, so it cannot establish that ESC actually alters how people drive.
No — in a longitudinal structural equation modelling study of Danish healthcare workers, the relationship between leadership and employees' sleep quality was not mediated by employees' self-efficacy.

Direct relationships between transformational leadership and sleep quality were found; this relationship was negative cross-sectionally at both time points, but positive between baseline and follow-up.

Structural equation modelling was used to investigate the relationships between transformational leadership, self-efficacy and sleep quality at both time points independently (cross-sectionally) and longitudinally, with data collected from Danish healthcare workers at time 1 in 2005 (n = 447) and 18 months later at time 2 in 2007 (n = 274).

Because the mediation test was based on a longitudinal observational design rather than an experimental manipulation, the reported absence of a self-efficacy mediation pathway describes an association structure over time and does not establish that changing leadership behaviours would change sleep quality.

In a series of 20 patients who had both mitral and aortic prostheses and a diagnosis of PVE, surgery was undertaken in 17 patients (85%), and in 13 patients only the prosthetic valve that seemed infected was replaced.

The evidence on the safety of replacing only the apparently infected valve in double-prosthesis prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) is mixed: among the 13 patients in whom only the prosthetic valve that seemed infected was replaced, four died within a week after the procedure, whereas nine survived the operation, completed a course of antimicrobial therapy and were followed up for 15.78 months (95% CI: 12.83-18.72), with all nine considered cured and no relapses observed.

Routine insertion of an endoscopic nasobiliary drainage (ENBD) tube after endoscopic clearance of common bile duct stones was not necessary in patients with choledocholithiasis-induced acute cholangitis, because in a prospective randomized study of 104 such patients who underwent primary endoscopic treatment (51 ENBD, 53 no-ENBD), baseline clinical characteristics were similar between the groups and there was no significant difference in recurrence of cholangitis at 24 weeks (3.9% with ENBD vs 3.8% without ENBD; P =.99).

Routine ENBD insertion after clearance of common bile duct stones did not affect length of hospital stay in the same randomized comparison: 7.9 days (standard error = 1.2) in the ENBD group versus 7.9 days (standard error = 0.7) in the no-ENBD group (P =.98).

Routine insertion of an ENBD tube carried a procedural and patient burden: compared with the no-ENBD group, procedure time was longer (26.2 minutes [SE = 1.8] vs 22.7 minutes [SE = 1.0]; P =.01) and the discomfort score was higher (4.9 [SE = 0.4] vs 2.8 [SE = 0.3]; P =.02) in the ENBD group.

In a mouse study of T cells and toluene, T-cell deficiency was associated with altered spatial learning after toluene exposure, but the reported evidence is mixed: nude (T-cell-deficient) mice exposed to 90 ppm toluene showed a longer escape latency on days 3 and 4 of the acquisition phase than corresponding wild-type mice, whereas the effect of toluene on escape latency was not significant in nude mice, and no significant difference between groups was found in the reversal phase.

The evidence comes from animals rather than patients: eight-week-old male wild-type and nude BALB/c mice were exposed to toluene at 0, 9 and 90 ppm in a nose-only exposure chamber for 30 min per day for 3 consecutive days and then once per week for 4 weeks, and spatial learning was examined 24 hours after the completion of exposure using the Morris water maze apparatus.

The cited evidence indicates that prostate specific antigen does not need to be adjusted for body mass index: in 994 men (4,937 observations) without prostate cancer in the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging, body mass index was not significantly associated with prostate specific antigen after adjusting for age (p = 0.06), and a 10-point body mass index increase corresponded to a prostate specific antigen difference of only -0.03 ng/ml (95% CI -0.40-0.49).

In the same longitudinal aging study, results were similar when men with prostate cancer were included, when percent body fat was substituted for body mass index, and after adjusting for prostate volume, and longitudinal weight changes also had no significant association with prostate specific antigen; separate models explored men with prostate cancer censored at diagnosis, percent body fat measurements, weight changes with time, and adjustment for initial prostate size in 483 men (2,523 observations) with pelvic magnetic resonance imaging measurements.

In a separate cohort of 6,103 men who had a 2-year biopsy, of whom 1,646 (27%) were normal weight, 3,209 (53%) overweight and 1,248 (20%) obese, mean adjusted prostate specific antigen for normal weight, overweight and obese subjects was 7.73, 7.17 and 6.79 ng/ml on placebo (p-trend = 0.192) and 3.16, 2.93 and 2.62 ng/ml on dutasteride (p = 0.008).

In that study, AUC analysis using raw prostate specific antigen data for predicting prostate cancer ranged from 0.60 to 0.64 in the placebo arm and 0.58 to 0.66 in the dutasteride arm with no difference across body mass index categories (p-interactions ≥ 0.212), and similar results were found for high grade prostate cancer with AUC ranging from 0.69 to 0.70 in the placebo arm and 0.65 to 0.75 in the dutasteride arm but no differences across body mass index categories (p-interactions ≥ 0.157).

Yes — in a questionnaire-based survey of patients attending six rural and 11 regional general practices in New South Wales across 18 teaching sessions in November 2008, 118 of 122 patients consented to medical student involvement in their consultation, of whom 117 (99%) completed a pre-consultation survey and 100 (85%) a post-consultation survey, and patients were overwhelmingly positive about their doctor and practice being involved in student teaching and felt they themselves played an important role.

Before their consultation, patients expressed reluctance to allow students to conduct some or all aspects of the consultation independently, but after the consultation they reported they would have accepted higher levels of involvement than actually occurred.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: prediction of polymyalgia rheumatica prognosis at disease onset.

The cited single study supports biomolecular identification of allergenic pollen as a feasible new perspective for aerobiological monitoring: it aimed to verify the feasibility of a real-time PCR approach, as an alternative to optical analysis, for rapid, accurate and automated detection and quantification of airborne allergenic pollen taxa.
Current aerobiological monitoring systems rely on a morphologic identification approach that is time-consuming and may limit the expansion of sampling networks.

In this study, the traditional cetyl trimethyl ammonium bromide (CTAB)-based method was modified for DNA isolation from pollen, and the resulting modified DNA extraction protocol yielded good-quality pollen DNA.

Taxon-specific DNA sequences were identified through bioinformatics or literature searches and PCR amplified from the matching allergenic taxa, and complementary or degenerate TaqMan probes were developed from the sequences of the PCR products; taxon-specific nuclear gene fragments were also identified and sequenced.

The designed primer pairs and probes identified the selected pollen taxa, mostly at the required classification level, and pollen was properly identified even when it was collected on routine aerobiological tape.
Preliminary quantification assays on pollen grains were successfully performed on the test species and in mixes.

Irritable bowel syndrome is not a diagnosis of exclusion: guidelines emphasize that IBS is not a diagnosis of exclusion and encourage clinicians to make a positive diagnosis using the Rome criteria alone, and in a survey of nurse practitioners, primary care physicians, community gastroenterologists and IBS experts, experts were less likely than nonexperts to endorse IBS as a diagnosis of exclusion (8% vs 72%; P<0.0001); providers who did believe IBS is a diagnosis of exclusion ordered 1.6 more tests and consumed US$364 more than others (P<0.0001).

In a retrospective single-institution analysis of 692 women at 24-32 weeks' gestation who received antenatal corticosteroids (AC), continuation of pregnancy was short in most cases: 321 (46.4%) delivered within 1 week of AC, 92 of those women (13.3%) within 24 hours, and only 124 (17.9%) remained pregnant 1 week after AC and delivered before 34 weeks.
Two hundred forty-seven of the 692 women (35.7%) delivered at 34 weeks' gestation or later.

The study was designed to determine the duration of continuing pregnancy after AC administration and to evaluate the potential opportunity for rescue AC; the 124 women who remained pregnant 1 week after AC and delivered before 34 weeks were compared with women who delivered more than 2 weeks after AC but at 34 weeks or later.

Women were more likely to deliver before 34 weeks if they had received AC for premature preterm rupture of membranes (OR 3.83, 95% CI 2.06-7.17), for twins (OR 2.90, 95% CI 1.42-5.95), or before 28 weeks' gestation (OR 2.21, 95% CI 1.38-3.52).

Because this was a retrospective observational analysis, the reported proportions describe the timing of delivery after the initial AC course and identify a potential window for rescue AC; they cannot establish that administering a rescue course improves outcomes.

To ascertain the perspectives of Trainee Ophthalmologist Diplomats (TOD) on the Ophthalmic Diploma Training (ODT) in West Africa with a view to improving the programme, a survey of set 2005 TOD on ODT was carried out in Ghana, 2006.
Nine trainees (75.0%) felt the programme was well structured, training allowances were adequate eight (66.7%) and inadequate four (33.3%).
Eleven (91.7%) trainees would work wherever they were posted; ten (83.3%) trainees had sense of fulfillment and three (25%) would like to proceed for residency training.
All trainees were at least good in chalazion surgery and treatment of common medical eye conditions.
Majority were at least good in eye surgery like cataract, eleven (91.7%); trabeculectomy nine (75.0%); pterygium 10 (83.3%); eyelid, eight (66.7%); destructive 11 (91.6%) and refraction 9 (75.0%).
Some trainees' perceived problems included inadequate sponsorship (33.3%), short duration of the course four (33.3%) and poor accommodation facility two (16.7%).
However, trainees' suggested increase in training posts, four (33.3); training allowance three (25.0%); and incentives for trainers/training hospitals two (16.7%).

Because the evidence comes from a survey of one cohort of trainees' self-reported perspectives, it documents perceived strengths, problems and suggested changes in the programme; it does not measure whether implementing those suggested changes would improve training or trainee competence.

The trial of fenofibrate in sleep apnoea was a proof-of-concept study consisting of a placebo run-in period of 1 week (5 weeks if fibrate washout was required) followed by a 4-week randomized, double-blind treatment period, in which 34 subjects with diagnosed sleep apnoea syndrome not treated with continuous positive airways pressure (mean age 55 years, BMI 34 kg/m2, fasting triglycerides 3.5 mmol/L) were randomized to once-daily fenofibrate 145 mg NanoCrystal tablet or placebo; overnight polysomnography, computerized attention/vigilance tests and blood sampling for lipids, insulin, fasting plasma glucose and fibrinogen were performed at the end of each study period, and because the study was exploratory a range of sleep variables was evaluated.

The investigators characterized the design as an exploratory study in patients with mild to moderate sleep apnoea with limited treatment duration, concomitant hypnotic treatment in 35% of patients and no correction for multiplicity of testing.
Fenofibrate produced no significant change in the apnoea/hypopnoea index, with a reduction versus control of 14% (95% CI -47 to 40%, p = 0.533).

Fenofibrate significantly reduced the percentage of time with SpO(2)<90%, from 9.0% to 3.5% compared with 10.0% to 11.5% on placebo (p = 0.007), and reduced obstructive apnoeas by 44%, from 18.5 at baseline to 15.0 at end of treatment versus 29.0 to 30.5 on placebo (p = 0.048), as well as non-cortical micro-awakenings per hour, from 23.5 to 18.0 versus 24.0 to 25.0 with placebo (p = 0.004).
Other sleep variables evaluated in the trial were not significantly influenced by fenofibrate.
The retrieved evidence on halofantrine and ototoxicity comes only from guinea pig cochlear histology; it does not establish that halofantrine causes hearing loss or hearing impairment in humans.

In that study, 30 guinea pigs were divided into a control group, a halofantrine therapeutic dose group and a halofantrine double therapeutic dose group, with one cochlea per animal stained with haematoxylin and eosin and the other with toluidine blue.
No changes were detected in the control group.
The halofantrine therapeutic dose group showed loss and distortion of inner hair cells and inner phalangeal cells, and loss of spiral ganglia cells.
In the halofantrine double therapeutic dose group, the inner and outer hair cells were distorted and there was loss of spiral ganglia cells.

The authors state that there have been no studies investigating halofantrine's effect on hearing, and the drug's introduction has been delayed because of possible side effects and insufficient studies of adverse reactions in humans.

Because the reported findings are histological changes in guinea pig cochleae rather than audiometric or functional hearing measurements in humans, they cannot by themselves establish that halofantrine causes hearing loss or hearing impairment in patients.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Hearing loss or hearing impairment in humans.

The cited evidence supports monitoring temperature during kidney allograft preservation: although grafts are generally considered to be preserved at 4 degrees C during cold storage, the authors state that actual temperature conditions are not known, and direct monitoring showed markedly different temperature profiles between storage containers.

Temperature was monitored with the Thermobouton probe during preservation of pig kidneys under the same conditions used with human grafts, with the probe recording the temperature level every 10 minutes over four days.

The study also examined the best probe position for monitoring and the effect of ice quantity: temperature levels were the same regardless of probe position within the transport pack, and were similar when 2 or 4 kg of crushed ice were used.

With the new Biotainer storage can and Vitalpack transport pack, the lowest temperature was maintained for 15 hours and the temperature stayed below 5 degrees C for 57 hours, whereas the former storage can maintained its lowest temperature level for 80 minutes and reached 5 degrees C after 10 hours 40 minutes.
Similar temperature results were observed when the conservation of actual human kidney grafts, harvested at the authors' institution between August 2007 and May 2008, was monitored.

As a limitation entailed by the reported design, the study measured temperature levels only during preservation (in pig kidneys under conditions matching human grafts, with human graft monitoring reported as similar) and did not report transplant or graft outcomes, so it cannot establish that temperature monitoring itself improves clinical outcomes.

The cited evidence is mixed on whether it is appropriate to implant kidneys from elderly donors into young recipients: among 91 consecutive transplants of cadaver kidneys from donors older than 60 years implanted into recipients younger than 60 years, compared with 91 matched transplants in which both donor and recipient were younger than 60 years, patient, graft and death-censored graft survival did not differ significantly over 10 years, but serum creatinine was significantly higher in the elderly-donor group.
Patient survival at 1, 5 and 10 years was 97.6%, 87.2% and 76.6% in the elderly-donor/younger-recipient group versus 98.8%, 87.5% and 69.5% in the control group (P=0.642).

Graft survival at 1, 5 and 10 years was 92.9%, 81.3% and 64.2% in the elderly-donor/younger-recipient group versus 93.9%, 76.4% and 69.5% in the control group (P=0.980), and graft survival with death censored was 94.4%, 92.6% and 77.4% versus 94.3%, 86.7% and 84.4% (P=0.747).
Creatininaemias at 1, 5 and 10 years were 172, 175 and 210 in the elderly-donor/younger-recipient group versus 139, 134 and 155 in the control group (P<0.05).

The two groups did not differ with regard to recipient age, sex, cause of death and renal function of the donor, hepatitis C and cytomegalovirus serologies, cold ischemia time, tubular necrosis, immediate diuresis, need for dialysis, human leukocyte antigen incompatibilities, hypersensitized patients, acute rejection, waiting time on dialysis, and days of admission.

Because the report compares consecutive transplants with a matched control group rather than randomising donor kidneys, it can describe the association between donor age and 10-year outcomes in recipients younger than 60 years but cannot by itself establish that donor age causes the observed differences.

Among 328 residents responding (77% of 424 surveyed residents from 11 residency programs at three academic medical institutions), 41% of men versus 27% of women planned to have children during residency (P =.01), and after adjusting for age, institution, postgraduate year, and knowledge of parental leave policies, women were less likely than men to plan to have children during residency (odds ratio 0.46, 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.84).

Because the survey measured intentions to have children during residency rather than the actual timing of pregnancies or childbirth, the evidence does not establish that women residents actually delayed childbearing.

The instrument measured four career threats of having children during residency - extended training, loss of fellowship positions, pregnancy complications, and interference with career plans - on a five-point Likert scale, and compared with men, women had higher scores for each item and a higher mean score (2.9 versus 2.1, P =.001), signifying greater belief in the potential of pregnancy to threaten careers.
In mediation analysis, threats to career explained 67% of the gender variance.

Because the study assessed plans/intentions to have children during residency rather than actual childbearing, the mediation result does not establish that actual childbearing delay is attributable to perceived career threats.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: actual delay in childbearing.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: actual childbearing delay attributable to perceived career threats.

Yes — in a study of 164 obese and 94 normal-weight individuals, phagocytic NADPH oxidase activity and plasma leptin levels were both enhanced (P<0.05) in obese patients compared with controls, and NADPH oxidase activity correlated positively with leptin in obese patients.
The association between phagocytic NADPH oxidase activity and leptin in obese patients remained significant in a multivariate analysis.
In-vitro experiments in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells and murine macrophages showed that leptin induced NADPH oxidase activation.

Inhibition of the leptin-induced NADPH oxidase activity by wortmannin and bisindolyl maleimide suggested a direct involvement of the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase and protein kinase C pathways, respectively.
Leptin-induced NADPH oxidase activation promoted macrophage proliferation.

Because the human evidence linking leptin to phagocytic NADPH oxidase activity in obesity is a cross-sectional association, it cannot by itself establish that lowering leptin improves clinical outcomes; the supporting mechanistic data come from in-vitro cell experiments rather than patient interventions.
One hundred and nine residents (109) were included in the study; 68 (6239%) were male and 41 (37.61%) were female with a mean age of 26 years.
Only 6 residents (5.50%) practiced physical activity according to international guidelines (more than three times a week for more than 30 minutes each time).

Most residents (n = 76 ; 69.73%) used to skip one or two meals especially breakfast and as a consequence 30 male (44.11%) and 4 female (9.75%) students were overweight, with a statistical difference between the two sexes (Fisher test, p-value = 0.001).

Twenty-eight residents (25.69%) were smokers with a male predominance, and 14 residents of both genders (12.84%) drank alcohol regularly (>3 times a week) while 71 (65.14%) had a drink occasionally (once a month or less).

In the same cohort of first-year residents at Hôtel-Dieu de France, only 25 residents (23%) had a complete and up-to-date immunization status, and the immunization gap was basically against measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) and diphtheria, tetanus, poliomyelitis (dT Polio).
Ninety-nine residents (90.83%) had full immunization against hepatitis B, with an adequate response documented in 78 residents (71.56%).

The evidence indicates that these future doctors were not consistently applying prevention rules to themselves: only 6 residents (5.50%) met international physical activity guidelines and only 25 residents (23%) of the cohort had a complete and up-to-date immunization status, with the immunization gap basically against MMR and dT Polio.

The study design was a review of the medical files of all first-year medicine and surgery residents at the academic hospital Hôtel-Dieu de France between 2005 and 2008 who attended a preventive medical visit at the University Center of Family and Community Health, so the reported health practices and vaccination status describe this single-institution resident cohort and cannot be generalized to a nationally representative population of medical students, for which no such survey existed.

In Texas during 1995-2005, African-American and Hispanic women generally experienced higher breast cancer mortality than White non-Hispanics, with these differences especially significant in the southeast metropolitan areas and the southwest border of Texas.

Geographic scale mattered for detecting racial disparities in breast cancer mortality: the proportion and location of significant disparities changed depending on the type of statistic used (relative risk versus risk difference) and the geographic level examined (census tract, zip code, or county).
The largest proportion of significant results was observed for the risk difference statistic combined with census tract data.

Racial disparities were quantified using both relative (RR) and absolute (RD) statistics that account for population size and correct for the unreliable rates typically observed for minority groups and smaller geographic units.

The evidence is mixed: in a survey of all Dutch hospitals conducted in winter 2007/2008 and analysed with descriptive statistics and structural equation modelling, adoption of case-mix based reimbursement within hospitals' budgeting processes stimulated hospitals to establish care programmes through the use of process-oriented performance measures, yet implementation of those care programmes was not (yet) accompanied by a change in focus from function (delivery of independent care activities) to process (delivery of care activities as a connected chain of interdependent care activities).

The study framed its question around whether case-mix based reimbursement stimulates development of care coordination via care programmes and a process-oriented way of working, noting that such reimbursement is believed to push management and clinicians to reduce quality problems such as waiting times and poor coordination, and that while many studies show greater efficiency, it remained unclear whether care coordination improved.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: a change in focus from function to process in care delivery (care activities delivered as a connected chain of interdependent activities).

The evidence is mixed on whether hypoalbuminemia is an independent prognostic factor in gastric cancer: in one cohort serum albumin lost statistical independence after multivariate adjustment, whereas in two other series low serum albumin remained independently correlated with prognosis.

In a Glasgow cohort of patients with gastric carcinoma, most of the patients had stage III/IV disease and received palliative treatment; the minimum follow-up was 15 months, and during follow-up 157 (72%) patients died of their cancer.

In that cohort, univariate analysis found stage (p<0.001), treatment (p<0.001), albumin level (p<0.001) and CRP level (p<0.001) to be significant predictors of survival; on multivariate analysis stage (p<0.001), treatment (p<0.001) and CRP level (p<0.001) remained significant predictors, and albumin was no longer an independent predictor of survival.

In a separate gastric cancer series, low levels of serum albumin, advanced TNM stage, presence of venous invasion, and high CEA levels were independently correlated with prognosis in multivariate analysis.

In a third series of gastric cancer patients, among the sixteen variables of univariate analysis, five were identified to have prognostic significance: performance status (p<0.001), stage (p=0.001), diabetes mellitus (p=0.005), serum albumin (p<0.001) and hemoglobin levels (p=0.03); multivariate analysis showed performance status, stage and serum albumin level to be independent prognostic factors for survival (p=0.02, p=0.02 and p=0.009 respectively), but diabetes mellitus was not an independent factor.

The finding that albumin was no longer an independent predictor in the Glasgow cohort came from multivariate adjustment within that observational cohort, so it indicates that the apparent prognostic value of albumin in that dataset was not independent of the other factors analyzed, rather than showing that albumin measurement has no prognostic association.

Yes — in three studies in which 608 students were randomly assigned to receive either a perspective-taking instruction or a neutral instruction before a clinical skills examination in 2006–2007, intervention students outscored controls on standardized patient (SP) satisfaction in every study, with SP satisfaction as the main outcome in all three: Study 1 (245 third-year medical students, two universities) P =.01, standardized effect size = 0.16; Study 2 P =.001, standardized effect size = 0.31; Study 3 (258 third-year medical students, two universities) P =.009, standardized effect size = 0.13.

Study 2 (105 physician assistant students at one university), which extended Study 1 to examine generalizability across student and SP subpopulations, found that perspective-taking improved African American SPs' satisfaction.

Study 3, which examined the intervention's effect among students with high versus low baseline perspective-taking tendencies, found that intervention students with high baseline tendencies outscored controls (P =.0004, standardized effect size = 0.25), whereas those with low baseline tendencies did not (P =.72, standardized effect size = 0.00).

In a study of 66 children classified by Rome III criteria into a constipated group (n = 35; mean age 6.8 ± 2.9 years) and a control group (n = 31; mean age 8.4 ± 3.8 years), pelvic ultrasonography was performed after clinical evaluation by 2 separate radiologists: bladder capacity and transverse rectal diameter were measured with a full bladder, and then rectal diameter and rectal anterior wall thickness were measured and the presence of fecal load in the rectum and sigmoid colon was recorded with an empty bladder.
Comparison of the ultrasonographic measurements of the 2 radiologists showed no interobserver difference (r = 0.981; P<.001).

The posturination mean rectal diameter was thicker in the constipated group (3.02 ± 1.04 cm) than in the control group (1.98 ± 0.64 cm) (P<.001), and rectal anterior wall thickness and fecal load were higher in the constipated patients (P<.001).
The cutoff point of rectal diameter for a diagnosis of constipation was determined as 2.44 cm, with 71% sensitivity, 76% specificity, and an area under the curve of 0.825 (P<.001).
For follow-up, the examination and ultrasound were repeated after treatment for a month in these patients.

After treatment for a month there was a significant decrease in the constipation score and fecal load (P<.001), but the rectal diameter had not reached normal limits despite the decrease, measuring 2.71 ± 0.77 cm (P>.05).

Lifetime prevalence of impetigo appears increased in children with atopic dermatitis: in a population-based cross-sectional study of 1117 children aged 0-6 years attending nursery schools in Ishigaki City, Okinawa Prefecture, Japan, multiple logistic regression showed the odds of having a history of impetigo contagiosum were 1.8 times higher in AD children than in non-AD children.
Among the 913 children analysed (132 with AD), a history of impetigo contagiosum, molluscum contagiosum or herpes virus infection was reported in 45.1%, 19.7% and 2.5% of children, respectively.
Because the study was cross-sectional, it cannot establish that atopic dermatitis causes these infections.

Lifetime prevalence of molluscum contagiosum was not increased in children with atopic dermatitis: a history of molluscum contagiosum was significantly correlated with male gender, but not with a personal history of atopic dermatitis.
Lifetime prevalence of herpes virus infection was not increased in children with atopic dermatitis: no correlated factors were found for herpes virus infection in this study.

In a retrospective multicenter study of 12 patients with spinal cord sarcoidosis accompanied by compressive cervical myelopathy who underwent decompressive surgery, the procedure showed limited effectiveness: postoperative recovery rates in the surgery group were -7.4% at 1 week and -1.1% at 4 weeks, and the recovery rate of the Japanese Orthopedic Association score, which increased after steroid therapy, was lower in the surgery group (18.6%) than in the nonsurgery group (62.5%), with a significant difference (P<0.01).
Only 5 cases showed clinical improvement, and the condition of these 5 patients had worsened again at an average of 7.4 weeks after surgery.

A total of 12 patients (0.08% of cervical myelopathy) were identified from the Nagoya Spine Group database as having spinal cord sarcoidosis treated with decompressive surgery; the Nagoya Spine Group database included 1560 cases with cervical myelopathy treated with cervical laminectomy or laminoplasty from 2001 to 2005.
As control subjects, 8 patients with spinal cord sarcoidosis without a compressive lesion who underwent high-dose steroid therapy without surgery were recruited.
Postoperative oral steroid therapy was initiated at an average of 6.4 weeks, and the average initial dose was 54.0 mg in the surgery group, while it was 51.3 mg in the nonsurgery group.

The study design was a retrospective multicenter case series with a separately recruited nonsurgical control group, so the comparison of groups cannot establish that decompressive surgery itself causes worse neurological recovery.

Yes — in NHANES III adults, waist circumference (WC) and hip circumference (HC) were associated with height once models were adjusted for age and race, with WC scaling to height with mean (±SEE) powers of 0.76 ± 0.08 in men and 0.80 ± 0.05 in women, and HC with powers of 0.45 ± 0.05 in men and 0.53 ± 0.04 in women (all P<0.001).

The study analyzed adult non-Hispanic white, non-Hispanic black, and Mexican American men (n = 7422) and nonpregnant women (n = 7999) from NHANES III who had complete demographic and anthropometric data, and the univariate circumference-height models in this sample were weak or nonsignificant before age and race were taken into account.
Age- and race-adjusted incremental increases in the circumferences ranged from 0.2 to 0.5 cm per centimeter increase in height.
Both WC/height and HC/height scaled negatively to height in men and in women, whereas WC/HC scaled negatively to height in women only (all P<0.001).
Models additionally controlling for self-reported health status gave similar results to the age- and race-adjusted models.

The authors note that whether, and how, circumferences including WC and HC scale to height had remained unclear, and that clarifying this matters when developing normative ranges or applying WC/height and HC/height as risk indexes.
No, 'high-risk' HPV DNA was not detected in human breast milk in the cited study: of 32 studied human milk specimens, none contained 'high-risk' HPV 16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56 or 58 DNA.
The milk specimens were collected from 21 HPV-positive and 11 HPV-negative mothers and were evaluated for HPV infection using polymerase chain reaction techniques.
Yes, a possible role for fondaparinux as a bridging agent in the perioperative setting is explored, but anticoagulation guidelines provide minimal direction on the perioperative use of fondaparinux.

Fondaparinux's extended half-life of 17-21 hours complicates its use as a perioperative bridging therapy, and the ideal time for discontinuation before surgery is an issue, particularly in surgeries with a high bleeding risk or in which neuraxial anesthesia is used; professional anesthesia guidelines also conflict on the timing of drug administration with neuraxial catheter use, so it may be optimal to avoid fondaparinux use before surgery.
Guidance for perioperative bridging with fondaparinux must be derived from pharmacokinetic data, surgical prophylaxis trials, case reports, and anesthesia guidelines.

Published trials used fondaparinux sodium 2.5 mg daily for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in surgical patients, and the majority avoided its use before surgery in patients receiving neuraxial anesthesia.
Three case reports cited the use of fondaparinux sodium as perioperative bridge therapy; one used a 2.5-mg dose and the other two used a full treatment dose of 7.5 mg.

Fondaparinux may have a role in bridge therapy in instances where low-molecular-weight heparin or inpatient use of i.v. unfractionated heparin is not possible, is contraindicated, or has limited efficacy, such as in a patient with a history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia or antithrombin III deficiency.

Because the perioperative bridging guidance described rests on pharmacokinetic data, surgical prophylaxis trials, case reports, and anesthesia guidelines rather than dedicated comparative bridging trials, and the bridging experience cited consists of three case reports, this evidence cannot establish the efficacy or safety of fondaparinux as a perioperative bridge.

No — in a retrospective matched cohort of neonates undergoing major surgery for esophageal atresia (EA) or congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH), minimal access surgery (MAS) was not associated with less pain: cumulative opioid (median mg/kg (IQR)) doses did not differ significantly between MAS patients and controls at any of the time points assessed (12, 24, 48 h and 7 days postoperatively), and the same held true for postoperative pain scores.

At 24 h postoperatively, cumulative opioid doses were 0.84 (0.61–1.83) mg/kg in MAS versus 1.06 (0.60–1.36) mg/kg in controls for CDH patients (p=1.0), and 0.48 (0.30–0.75) mg/kg in MAS versus 0.49 (0.35–0.79) mg/kg in controls for EA patients (p=0.83).

The study group comprised 24 MAS patients (14 EA; 10 CDH), each matched to two controls, giving 48 control patients (28 EA; 20 CDH) matched on diagnosis, sex and age at surgery, with opioid titration based on validated pain scores (VAS and COMFORT behaviour) applied by protocol and group comparisons made with the Mann-Whitney test.

Because these findings come from a retrospective cohort with matched controls rather than a randomized comparison, the absence of a difference in opioid consumption and pain scores between MAS and conventional open surgery in neonates is an association that cannot by itself establish that either operative approach causes a change in postoperative pain.

Targeted educational interventions aimed at increasing patient awareness of clinical trials did not improve accrual: in a study at a cancer center, new patients referred over a 4-month period were mailed a baseline survey, then received educational interventions (an orientation session highlighting clinical trials, a pamphlet, and a reference to a clinical trials Web site), with a postintervention survey sent 3 months after the initial mailing.
Patient satisfaction with information significantly increased after the interventions, but there was no increase in subsequent enrollment in clinical trials.

Yes — the patient-safety curriculum delivered during a paediatric clerkship, in which medical students investigated medication errors, was associated with significant changes on questionnaire items related to patient safety attitudes.

In the curriculum, student groups identified and then analysed medication errors during their clinical rotation using the Learning From Defects framework to organise and present their findings; all 25 student groups identified, analysed and presented patient safety concerns.

Attitudinal outcomes were measured with questions derived from the Safety Attitudes Questionnaire, and the curriculum's effectiveness was demonstrated by significant changes on questionnaire items relating to patient safety attitudes.
A total of 108 students completed the curriculum between July 2008 and July 2009.

Yes — in women with pelvic organ prolapse (POP), defecatory symptoms are significantly more common in those with pelvic pain, based on a cross-sectional study of 248 women with stage II POP or greater.

In that POP cohort, the reported associations were straining with bowel movement (OR 2.4, 95% CI 1.3, 4.6), sense of incomplete emptying (OR 4.4, 95% CI 2.3, 8.2), pain with bowel movement (OR 5.3, 95% CI 1.2, 23.0) and splinting with bowel movement (OR 3.8, 95% CI 2.0, 7.5).

Women in this study were stratified into "pain" and "no-pain" groups according to their response to a question on the Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory short form, and associations between patient demographics, examination findings and validated questionnaire responses were evaluated.

Because the cited evidence comes from a cross-sectional design, the reported associations between pelvic pain and defecatory symptoms in women with POP cannot establish a causal direction between the two.

In a secondary analysis of 167 cancer patients referred for treatment of cancer-related pain, baseline pain intensity did not predict poor opioid response: no correlation was found between baseline pain intensity categories and opioid response.

Pain intensity at admission was recorded and patients were divided into three categories (mild, moderate, severe), while opioid response was classified into four levels, from (a) good pain control with minimal opioid escalation and without relevant adverse effects through (d) poor pain control with adverse effects.
Across these four response levels, 76, 44, 41 and 6 patients showed response a, b, c and d, respectively.

In a prospective study of preoperative staging of liver metastases of colorectal carcinoma (LMCRC), PET/CT added little over multidetector CT: in lesion-by-lesion hepatic staging the sensitivity of MDCT/MR was superior to PET/CT (89.2% vs 55%, p < 0.001), and on extrahepatic staging PET/CT was superior to MDCT/MR only for detection of locoregional recurrence (p = 0.03) and recurrence in uncommon sites (p = 0.016).

Between 2006 and 2008, 97 patients evaluated for resection of LMCRC were prospectively enrolled; preoperative workup included MDCT and PET/CT, and in 11 patients with liver steatosis or iodinated contrast allergy MR was also performed.
New findings at PET/CT resulted in a change in therapeutic strategy in 17 patients, but the additional information was correct in only eight cases and wrong in nine patients.

Because the study measured sensitivity, specificity and predictive values for hepatic and extrahepatic staging and the impact of new PET/CT findings on therapeutic strategy, its design supports conclusions about diagnostic performance and management change rather than about improved clinical outcomes from PET/CT-guided treatment.
The cited evidence does not establish that xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis (XGC) is a premalignant condition; the study explicitly states that the premalignant nature of this entity is not known.

In a comparison of surgically resected specimens (GBC 69 cases, XGC 65, chronic cholecystitis 18, control gallbladder 10), p53 mutation was positive in 52% of gallbladder carcinoma (GBC) cases and 3% of XGC cases, and was not expressed in chronic cholecystitis or control gallbladders; p53 expression was lower in XGC than in GBC (P<0.0001).

PCNA expression was seen in 65% of GBC cases and 11% of XGC cases, but not in chronic cholecystitis or control gallbladders, and was higher in GBC than in XGC (P=0.0001), while there was no significant difference between the XGC, chronic cholecystitis and control gallbladder groups.

Beta-catenin expression was positive in the GBC, XGC, chronic cholecystitis and control gallbladder groups, but the expression pattern in XGC, chronic cholecystitis and control gallbladders was homogenously membranous, whereas in GBC the membranous pattern was altered to cytoplasmic and nuclear.

Because the cited study is a cross-sectional immunohistochemical comparison of p53, PCNA and beta-catenin expression in resected GBC, XGC and inflammatory gallbladder specimens, it cannot by itself demonstrate that XGC undergoes malignant transformation or progresses to gallbladder cancer.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: direct evidence of malignant transformation or progression to gallbladder cancer.
Thirty-two ex-ELBW subjects (11 males [M] and 21 females [F], aged 17-29years, mean age 22.2 ± 2.3 years) were compared with 25 C (7 M and 18F).
ADMA levels were reduced in ex-ELBW subjects compared to C (0.606+0.095 vs 0.562+0.101 μmol/L, p<0.05).
ADMA levels were significantly correlated inversely with gestational age (r=-0.61, p<0.00001) and birth weight (r=-0.57, p<0.0002).
The retrieved evidence does not establish: prediction of early endothelial dysfunction by ADMA levels in young adults born preterm.

Yes — mitochondria do play a role in the developmentally regulated programmed cell death (PCD) that remodels lace plant (Aponogeton madagascariensis) leaves, since the cited in vivo work delineated mitochondrial dynamics during this PCD.

Using window-stage leaves (in which PCD is occurring) stained with the mitochondrial dye MitoTracker Red CMXRos and examined by live cell imaging, the study classified mitochondrial dynamics into four categories (M1–M4) on the basis of distribution, motility and membrane potential (ΔΨm).
A TUNEL assay revealed fragmented nuclear DNA in a gradient across these mitochondrial stages.

The potential importance of mitochondrial permeability transition pore (PTP) formation during PCD was tested only indirectly, by in vivo cyclosporine A (CsA) treatment; treated lace plant leaves had a significantly lower number of perforations than controls and showed mitochondrial dynamics resembling those of non-PCD cells.

In the Anglia region of England, 3406 cases of gynaecological cancer diagnosed from 1996 to 2003 were identified, survival was analysed by Cox proportional hazards regression relative to cases diagnosed in 1996, and survival was the primary endpoint.

Survival rates for cases diagnosed between 1996 and 1999 were broadly the same across that period, with a marked improvement taking place in 2000 and continuing to 2003, for all gynaecological sites combined (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.64-0.79, comparing 2000-03 with 1996-99 diagnoses).

Centralisation was reflected in the 1999 Department of Health 'Improving Outcomes in Gynaecological Cancer' guidance in England, which advised case management by multidisciplinary teams with surgical concentration in specialist hospitals; this guidance was rapidly adopted in the East of England, with a population of 2.5 million, and there was a concurrent change towards major surgery being performed in specialist centres from 2000.

Multidisciplinary management featured in the 1999 Department of Health guidance, which advised case management by multidisciplinary teams, and this guidance was rapidly adopted in the East of England.

The timing of the survival improvement coincided with the organisational changes: survival was broadly unchanged for 1996-1999 diagnoses, improved markedly from 2000 onwards, and there was a concurrent shift from 2000 towards major surgery being performed in specialist centres.
Adjustment for treatments or method of case follow-up did not attenuate the observed survival improvements.

The retrieved report is a time-trend survival analysis of cases diagnosed between 1996 and 2003, a design that can show that the survival improvement was concurrent with the adoption of centralised, multidisciplinary care but cannot by itself establish that centralisation of care or multidisciplinary management caused the improvement.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: a causal effect of centralisation of care and multidisciplinary management on the survival improvement.

This was a cost-utility study from a health care system's perspective comparing coformulated fixed dose (FXD) strategy versus multiple free dose combination (FRC) in antiretroviral therapy; the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS) was used to identify HIV/AIDS patients with ≥2 active antiretroviral medications.
Utility was measured using SF-6D scores from the SF-12 questionnaire.

Patients on FXD were matched in 1:1 ratio with the FRC group using propensity scores; on matching, 70 patients from FXD had a match from the FRC group, and no differences in sociodemographic and health status variables were observed between the matched groups.
The mean utility gained by using FXD over FRC was 0.085; however, this difference was not statistically significant.
Therefore, the cited evidence does not establish that combining antiretroviral agents in a single dosage form enhances quality of life in HIV/AIDS patients.

Because the quality-of-life comparison comes from a matched cost-utility analysis of survey data rather than a randomized trial, it cannot establish that adopting a single dosage form causes an improvement in quality of life.

In an analysis designed to determine which delivery channels are associated with the greatest reductions in under-5 mortality rates (U5MR), using data from sequential population-based surveys to examine the correlation between changes in coverage of clinical, outreach, and family and community services and in U5MR for 27 high-burden countries, the strongest correlation with reductions in U5MR was observed for access to clinical services (all countries: p = 0.02, r² = 0.58; 19 African countries: p < 0.001, r² = 0.67).

Because the analysis used average annual changes in coverage of 22 service variables and principal component analysis with linear regression to assess correlations with changes in under-5 mortality after controlling for potential confounders, the clinical-service finding is correlational and does not establish that improving clinical service access itself causes declines in child mortality.

For outreach activities, average annual change in U5MR was significantly correlated with antenatal care and family planning services, while average annual change in immunization services showed no association.

Because the analysis used average annual changes in coverage of 22 service variables and principal component analysis with linear regression to assess correlations with changes in under-5 mortality after controlling for potential confounders, the outreach findings are correlational and do not establish that improving outreach services itself causes declines in child mortality.

In the family- and community services domain, improvements in breastfeeding were associated with significant changes in mortality in the 30 countries but not in the African subset; while in the African countries, nutritional status improvements were associated with a significant decline in mortality.

Because the analysis used average annual changes in coverage of 22 service variables and principal component analysis with linear regression to assess correlations with changes in under-5 mortality after controlling for potential confounders, the family- and community-service findings are correlational and do not establish that improving these services itself causes declines in child mortality.

Among stroke survivors, Ministry of Transportation of Ontario (MTO) records and self-reports of motor vehicle collisions and driving convictions agreed only moderately, with a kappa coefficient of 0.52 for collisions and 0.47 for convictions.
In the same sample, MTO records did not match self-reports for 7 participants (13.5%) regarding collision involvement and for 9 participants (17.3%) regarding driving convictions.

Consulting both sources together identified up to 56 percent more accidents and up to 46 percent more convictions in the study population in the 5 years before study entry than when either source was used alone.

The comparison used the driving records of 56 moderately impaired stroke survivors without severe communication disorders who had been referred for a driving assessment and originally recruited for a prospective study on driving and community re-integration post-stroke; records covering the 5 years before study entry and the 1-year study period were obtained with written consent from the Ministry of Transportation of Ontario, Canada, while self-reports of collisions and convictions were collected by semistructured interview and then compared with the MTO records, and 43 participants completed the study.

The evidence is mixed: elderly and younger cancer patients differ in some care needs and treatment attitudes, but a cross-sectional survey of patients aged 35-82 (subgroups ≤65 vs ≥66 years) found few significant differences between the two age subgroups apart from issues such as the need for intimacy and support.

In that survey, the requests most frequently expressed by the older group were financial-insurance information (73.9%), the need to talk to people with the same illness (71.7%), the need for more comprehensible information from doctors and nurses (71.7%), and the need for better dialogue with clinicians (69.6%).

Because this needs survey was an observational cross-sectional study, its age-related differences in expressed needs describe associations and cannot establish that changing care delivery by age would improve outcomes.
In a comparison of cohorts aged <65 years and 65+ years, disease diagnosis differed between the cohorts (P<0.001) while treatment modalities were similar (P = 0.28).

There was no difference between the <65 and 65+ cohorts in the desire for surgery offering a chance of disease cure (P = 0.75), except that the elderly desired cure more when treatment was associated with disfigurement (P = 0.029).

Issues of sexuality and femininity associated with gynecologic cancer and treatment were more important to younger patients (P<0.001), whereas the elderly supported equality of care with relation to age more strongly than the young and believed more strongly that doctors should make management decisions (P<0.001).

Older patients with lung cancer are less likely to be offered surgery than younger patients, although the retrieved report does not provide the results of its comparison of symptom occurrence, severity, and distress between older (≥65 years) and younger (<65 years) patients prior to surgery.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: differences in symptom occurrence, severity, and distress between older and younger lung cancer patients prior to surgery.

For severely injured adult trauma patients (Injury Severity Score >15) in one Australian regional health service, trauma center level was associated with a mortality difference: patients presenting to a level III center had a significantly higher risk of death than those presenting to the level I center, regardless of age, sex, ISS, or prehospital time.

The analysis used NSW Institute of Trauma and Injury Management data for 2002-2007, covering 1,986 trauma presentations over the 6-year period; logistic regression was used for binary outcomes and multivariable linear regression for continuous outcomes, with sex, age, and ISS included as covariates in all models.
Peer review of deaths at the level III center identified problems in care delivery in 15 cases, associated with technical errors, delay in decision making, or errors of judgement.

Because the reported comparison is an observational association between the level of the center initially treating patients and mortality, it cannot establish that changing the level of treating center would itself improve patient outcomes.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: hospital length of stay by trauma center level.

In a post hoc analysis of an RCT of 190 prospectively enrolled average-risk screening colonoscopy patients (87 MiraLAX, 103 Golytely), the unadjusted adenoma detection rate was 26.2% (27/103) in the Golytely cohort versus 16.1% (14/87) with MiraLAX, a difference that did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.091); however, on multivariate analysis Golytely was 2.28 times more likely to be associated with adenoma detection (95% CI 1.05-4.98, P = 0.04) than MiraLAX.

In a retrospective review of 246 patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma and lung metastasis(es) alone presenting at diagnosis or as the first failure after primary treatment between 1993 and 2008 at an academic tertiary hospital, univariate and multivariate survival analyses of post-metastasis survival (PMS) and overall survival (OS) were performed to determine prognostic factors; age, disease-free interval (DFI) and treatment modality were independent prognostic factors for OS, whereas only age and treatment modality retained independent significance in the PMS analysis.

For the whole cohort of 246 patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma and lung metastasis alone, 3-year, 5-year and 10-year post-metastasis survival (PMS) was 34.3%, 17.0% and 8.6%, and corresponding overall survival (OS) was 67.8%, 45.4% and 18.5%.

Among patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma and lung metastasis alone, median post-metastasis survival was 45.6 months with combined therapy versus 23.7 months with chemotherapy alone, and median overall survival was 73.7 months versus 46.2 months, with the combined-therapy advantage statistically significant (P<0.001).

In stratified survival analysis, combined therapy benefited patients with a disease-free interval (DFI) greater than 1 year compared with chemotherapy alone, but did not benefit those with DFI of 1 year or less.

The evidence on combined modality treatment comes from a retrospective review of patients presenting at diagnosis or as first failure after primary treatment, so the reported survival differences between combined therapy and chemotherapy alone reflect an association in retrospectively compared groups rather than a randomized demonstration that combined therapy causes improved survival.
In a series of 68 patients with type 1 hepatorenal syndrome (HRS) associated with cirrhosis who were not candidates for liver transplantation, median survival was 13 days for the whole group.

Survival varied significantly with end-stage liver disease (ESLD) etiology in type 1 HRS: autoimmune 49 days, cardiac cirrhosis 22 days, idiopathic 15.5 days, viral 15 days, hepatitis C plus alcohol 14.5 days, alcohol 8 days, and neoplasia 4 days (p = 0.048).
The difference in survival between HRS associated with alcoholic liver disease and HRS from other etiologies was not statistically significant (p = 0.1).
Increased serum creatinine (p = 0.02) and urinary sodium of 6-10 mEq/l (p = 0.027) at the initiation of therapy were prognostic factors for mortality in type 1 HRS.

In the same cohort, HRS treatment modalities (p = 0.73), use of dialysis (p = 0.56), dialysis modality (p = 0.35), use of vasopressors (p = 0.26), pre-existing renal disease (p = 0.49), gender (p = 0.90) and age (p = 0.57) were not associated with survival.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: additional prognostic factors beyond ESLD etiology, serum creatinine, and urinary sodium 6-10 mEq/l in type 1 HRS.

The cited evidence does not demonstrate that growth hormone replacement reduces all-cause mortality in adults with growth hormone deficiency; in the treatment group of a Dutch nationwide cohort (n = 2229, monitored retrospectively 1985-2009), 95 patients died compared with 74.6 expected, giving a standardized mortality ratio of 1.27 (95% confidence interval 1.04-1.56), and the authors state that the effect of GH treatment on mortality remains to be established.

In the control groups of the same cohort (primary untreated, n = 109, and secondary partly treated, n = 356), mortality was not different from the background population, with expected mortality derived from cause-, sex-, calendar year- and age-specific national death and population counts.

Because the evidence comes from a retrospective observational registry cohort rather than a randomized comparison of treated versus untreated adults with growth hormone deficiency, it cannot establish that giving GH replacement reduces mortality.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: a demonstrated reduction in all-cause mortality with GH replacement compared with untreated/control GHD adults.

In patients with persistent atrial fibrillation, no significant correlation was found between left atrial regions showing sinus rhythm fractionation and those showing complex fractionated atrial electrograms recorded during atrial fibrillation (r =.2; P = NS), indicating that the two maps did not correspond.

The analysis was based on 20 patients (age 62 ± 9 years, 13 males) with persistent atrial fibrillation and 9 control subjects without organic heart disease or atrial fibrillation (age 36 ± 6 years, 4 males), all of whom underwent detailed left atrial electroanatomic mapping of complex fractionated atrial electrograms and sinus rhythm fractionation; the overlap of left atrial regions with CFAEs and SRF was compared within the AF population, the distribution of SRF was compared between patients with AF and normal controls, and propagation maps were analyzed to identify the activation patterns associated with sinus rhythm fractionation.
SRF regions (338 ± 150 points) and CFAE regions (418 ± 135 points) comprised 29% ± 14% and 25% ± 15% of the left atrial surface area, respectively.
Comparing patients with atrial fibrillation and controls, no significant difference was found in the distribution of sinus rhythm fractionation between the groups (P =.74).
Regions of sinus rhythm fractionation overlapped areas of wave-front collision 75% ± 13% of the time.
The aim of this study was to determine if educating residents about the potential effects of radiation exposure from computed tomographic (CT) imaging alters ordering patterns.
