Two to four months after a radiologist's lecture on the potential effects of radiation exposure related to CT scans, urology and orthopedic residents were surveyed regarding the number and types of CT scans they ordered, the use of alternative imaging modalities, and whether they used the lecture information to educate patients.
Twenty-one resident lecture attendants completed the survey.
The number of CT scans ordered after the lecture stayed constant for 90% (19 of 21) and decreased for 10% (two of 21).
The types of CT scans ordered changed after the lecture for 14% (three of 21).

Thirty-three percent (seven of 21) reported increases in alternative imaging after the lecture, including 24% (five of 21) reporting increases in magnetic resonance imaging and 19% (four of 21) reporting increases in ultrasound.

These results come from residents' survey responses about the number and types of CT scans they ordered, so they are self-reported ordering patterns; such an association does not by itself establish that the education caused the reported changes in CT ordering.

Yes, partly: in the Swiss National Cohort, men appeared to benefit more from being married than women with respect to mortality in middle age, but after adjustment for living arrangements the gender difference by marital status disappeared.

The benefit of being married was stronger for men than for women, yet mortality patterns were similar between genders, with higher mortality among divorced and single individuals than among widowed individuals below age 80.

The analysis used longitudinal Swiss National Cohort data linking 1990 census records to mortality data up to 2005 for all residents over age 44 years in Switzerland (n=2,440,242), with all-cause mortality hazard ratios for marital status and living arrangements estimated by Cox regression separately for men and women and different age groups, adjusted for education and socio-professional category.

Stratification by living arrangement showed the highest mortality risks among 45-64-year-old divorced men living alone (HR 1.72, 95% CI 1.67 to 1.76) and single men living alone (HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.63 to 1.71).
Among women of the same 45-64 age group, the highest mortality risk was observed for those who were single and living with a partner (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.58 to 1.82).
In older age groups the impact of marital status decreased.

As an observational census-linked cohort analysis, the reported hazard ratios describe associations between marital status, living arrangement and all-cause mortality and do not by themselves establish that changing marital status or living arrangement would alter mortality risk.

the authors evaluated in a randomized controlled trial the hypothesis that participation in a MSWM program does not predict outcomes after laparoscopic adjustable gastric banding (LAGB) in a publicly insured population.

Patients who met NIH consensus criteria for bariatric surgery and whose insurance did not require a mandatory 6-month MSWM program were randomized to a MSWM program with monthly visits over 6 months (individual or group) or usual care for 6 months and then followed for bariatric surgery outcomes postoperatively.
A total of 55 patients were enrolled in the study with complete follow-up on 23 patients.

No significant differences in weight loss and most patient behaviors were found between the two groups postoperatively, suggesting that participation in a MSWM program did not improve weight loss outcomes for LAGB.
Participation in a MSWM program did appear to have a positive effect on physical activity postoperatively.

In a cross-sectional household survey of women residing in rural areas and in their 0-12 months after childbirth from 30 rural townships, none of six dimensions and total score of quality of life displayed significant difference between women with normal delivery and caeserean section.
The overall caeserean section rate was 70·0% (962/1375), and most of them (59·7%) were selected by maternal request.

Postpartum quality of life was assessed with the scale for rural postnatal quality of life across six dimensions: physical complaints and pain, sleep and energy, sex satisfaction, interpersonal communication, self-evaluated living stress and perceived life satisfaction.

Because the study used a cross-sectional design, it can describe the absence of an association between delivery mode and postpartum quality of life but cannot establish that changing delivery mode would cause a change in women's postpartum quality of life.

In this single study, 32 animals (rabbits, the species proposed for surgical training) aged 3 to 5.5 months and weighing 3000 to 4200 g underwent different periods of preoperative fasting, exclusive intramuscular anesthesia with ketamine plus xylazine, and laparotomy with total gastrectomy and total splenectomy.

Preoperative (initial) and post-surgical (end) serum blood glucose were measured and gastric content was quantified after resection of the part; mean blood glucose was 199.4 mg/dl initially and 326.1 mg/dl at the end.
The anesthetic-surgical procedure carried a mortality rate of 3.125% (1 of 32) and a morbidity rate of 6.25% (2 of 32).

The cited evidence does not establish whether preoperative fasting is necessary or unnecessary, because the study assigned all animals to fasting periods and included no unfasted comparison group, so the effect of omitting fasting on gastric content or perioperative outcomes was not tested.

Despite extended fasting (a minimum of 2 hours of absolute fasting and a maximum of 8.5 hours for liquids and 20.5 hours for solids), all animals still presented gastric content at the end of the surgical procedure and a blood glucose increase.
When fasting for liquids and solids was compared with the quantity of solid gastric content, a moderate negative degree of correlation was found.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: omitting preoperative fasting affects gastric content or perioperative outcomes.

Yes — the cited evidence indicates that an advance care planning model was feasible in community palliative care, with three Victorian community palliative care services demonstrating that it was feasible to embed the Model into their organizational structures.

The finding comes from a multi-site action research study conducted over a 16-month period in 2007-2009 across three community palliative care services (one regional and two metropolitan services in Victoria, Australia).

Feasibility was assessed using mixed-method data collection: a baseline audit of staff and clients, analysis of relevant documents (client records, policies, procedures and quality improvement strategies) pre-implementation and post-implementation, and key informant interviews (n = 9).
In community settings, advance care planning conversations and involvement of family were treated as an important outcome measure rather than the completion rate of advance care planning documents.
The services adapted and applied their own concept of community, which widened the impact of the model.
Changes to quality audit processes were reported as essential to consolidate the model into routine palliative care practice.

Because the evidence comes from a multi-site action research study in three Australian community palliative care services rather than a controlled comparative design, the feasibility reported is limited to those participating services and does not establish effectiveness of the model elsewhere.

In a retrospective analysis of 35 patients treated by HIPEC with oxaliplatin or cisplatin, epidural analgesia for cytoreductive surgery was not associated with any reported spinal haematoma, meningitis or epidural abscess, but haemodynamic support was needed: norepinephrine was used in two subjects (6%) peroperatively and in four subjects (11%) during the 24 postoperative hours.
The median peroperative norepinephrine infusion rate in the two subjects who received it was 0.325 μg/kg per minute (range 0.32-0.33).

Before catheter removal, five subjects (14%) had a thrombopenia or a prothrombin time less than 60%, and two subjects (6%) had a leukopenia; no thrombopenia or blood coagulation disorders were recorded on the day of catheter removal.
The epidural catheter was used peroperatively before HIPEC in 12 subjects (34%) and after HIPEC in 23 subjects (66%).

Because the data come from a retrospective single-series analysis of 35 patients, the absence of spinal haematoma, meningitis and epidural abscess in this cohort cannot by itself establish an incidence rate or quantify the risk of the technique.

Yes — in a multicenter prospective cohort of individuals aged 55 and older without dementia attending European memory clinics, IADL disability helped predict dementia at both 1-year follow-up (OR = 2.20, 95% CI = 1.51-3.13) and 2-year follow-up (OR = 2.11, 95% CI = 1.33-3.33), in addition to the measured variables.

IADLs were measured using pooled activities from five informant-based questionnaires, and structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to investigate the relation between IADLs and dementia, with age, sex, education, depression, and cognitive measures (Mini-Mental State Examination and verbal memory) included in the model.

Participants with IADL disabilities at baseline had a higher conversion rate to dementia (24.4%) than participants without IADL disabilities (16.7%) (chi-square = 4.28, degrees of freedom = 1, P =.04).

Of 531 participants with baseline and 1-year follow-up assessments, 69 (13.0%) had developed dementia at 1-year follow-up, and at 2-year follow-up 481 participants were seen, of whom 100 (20.8%) had developed dementia.

Analysis of two nationally representative cross-sectional household surveys conducted in Kenya in 2003 and 2007, covering the public, private-not-for-profit and private-for-profit sectors, found that all three sectors recorded similar levels of pro-rich distribution in 2003, but by 2007 the private-not-for-profit sector was pro-poor, public sector benefits showed an equal distribution, and the private-for-profit sector remained pro-rich; larger pro-rich disparities were recorded for inpatient compared with outpatient benefits at the hospital level, while primary health care services were pro-poor.

Universal coverage involves ensuring that health care benefits are distributed on the basis of need for care and not on ability to pay; in the Kenyan health system assessed in this study, benefits were distributed on the basis of ability to pay and not on need for care, indicating that the distribution did not meet the principles of universal coverage.

Among 3,917 breast, colorectal and lung cancer Medicaid patients in Washington State diagnosed between 1997 and 2003, later stage at diagnosis for breast cancer patients was associated with travel burden, with an odds ratio of 1.488 per 100 driving miles (P =.037) and 1.270 per driving hour (P =.016), where driving distance and time were measured from patient residence to primary care provider.

Because these estimates come from regression models fitted to observational data on stage at diagnosis, they demonstrate an association and cannot establish that reducing travel burden would improve stage at diagnosis.

In the same Medicaid cohort, time-to-treatment after colorectal cancer diagnosis (days between diagnosis and surgery) was also associated with travel burden, increasing by 14.57 days per 100 driving miles (P =.002) and by 5.86 days per driving hour (P =.018).
The retrieved evidence does not establish: lung cancer-specific association between distance/travel burden and timely diagnosis or treatment.

The cited evidence does not establish that mesopic pupil size can be measured with a cobalt blue light slit-lamp biomicroscopy method: the study of slit-lamp biomicroscopy-based measurement (SLBM) assessed pupil diameter in general and did not report mesopic conditions or cobalt blue light illumination.

In 40 healthy eyes, two examiners took three repeated measurements with each instrument; mean pupil diameter was 5.81 ± 0.70 mm with SLBM versus 6.26 ± 0.68 mm with Colvard infrared pupillometry (CIP) when averaging both examiners' results (p = 0.01).
Mean differences between SLBM and CIP were -0.60 mm and -0.30 mm for the two examiners using the average of three readings (p = 0.02), and were very similar using the first reading.
Intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.97 and 0.92 for SLBM, compared with 0.96 and 0.90 for CIP.
For detection of pupils larger than 6 mm, SLBM sensitivity ranged from 55.56% to 73.68% and specificity from 76.19% to 95.45%.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: mesopic pupil size specifically and cobalt blue light slit-lamp biomicroscopy conditions are not reported.

The cited evidence indicates that performance in selection processes has limited ability to predict performance as a dental student: in a longitudinal review of admissions data for students entering dental education at the University of Otago, New Zealand between 2004 and 2009, pre-admission academic average, UMAT scores and interview performance did not predict performance as a dental student after controlling for variables.

In the Irish setting, where entry to university dental education is based solely on academic performance in the Leaving Certificate Examination, there was a significant relationship between Leaving Certificate performance and the First Dental Examination (correlation coefficient = 0.22, P<0.05), but this relationship explained only 12% of the variation in students' performance in that examination; there was no relationship between Leaving Certificate performance and the Final Dental Examination (correlation coefficient = 0.09, P>0.05).

Leaving Certificate Examination performance showed a significant correlation with performance in only seven of the 55 programme modules, all of which were pre-clinical modules and five of which were related to basic sciences.

In a rabbit model, partial expander deflation immediately before radiotherapy aggravated the tissue effects of irradiation: Group I received radiotherapy with full expanders, whereas Group II had expanders partially deflated immediately prior to radiotherapy, and a significant increase in skin blood flow was detected in Group II.

Histopathologic examination of biopsy specimens taken from different locations (skin, capsule and pocket floor) in each group revealed aggravated findings of chronic radiodermatitis in Group II, namely epidermal atrophy, dermal inflammation and fibrosis, neovascularisation, vascular changes and increased capsule thickness, especially around the lower expander pole.

The evidence for deflation-related exacerbation of radiotherapy effects comes from an animal experiment: eighteen New Zealand rabbits were divided into three groups, and 250 cc metallic port integrated anatomic breast expanders were implanted on the back of each animal with controlled expansion performed, so the reported aggravation applies to this animal model rather than to human two-stage breast reconstruction.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Exacerbation of radiotherapy adverse effects by partial expander deflation in human two-stage breast reconstruction.

the authors developed a decision analysis model comparing the cost-utility of three strategies to identify GDM: 1) no screening, 2) current screening practice (1-h 50-g glucose challenge test between 24 and 28 weeks followed by 3-h 100-g glucose tolerance test when indicated), or 3) screening practice proposed by the IADPSG.

Assumptions included that 1) women diagnosed with GDM received additional prenatal monitoring, mitigating the risks of preeclampsia, shoulder dystocia, and birth injury; and 2) GDM women had opportunity for intensive postdelivery counseling and behavior modification to reduce future diabetes risks.
The primary outcome measure was the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER).
The model demonstrates that the IADPSG recommendations are cost-effective only when postdelivery care reduces diabetes incidence.
For every 100,000 women screened, 6,178 quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) are gained, at a cost of $125,633,826.
The ICER for the IADPSG strategy compared with the current standard was $20,336 per QALY gained.
When postdelivery care was not accomplished, the IADPSG strategy was no longer cost-effective.
These results were robust in sensitivity analyses.

Because the analysis is a decision model whose stated assumptions include that women diagnosed with GDM received additional prenatal monitoring and had opportunity for intensive postdelivery counseling and behavior modification, the cost-effectiveness conclusion is conditional on those modeled assumptions rather than on observed clinical outcomes.

The cited evidence does not establish that pictorial warning labels on cigarette packages reduce smoking-related health disparities in smoking behavior or health outcomes across education or socioeconomic groups; the relevant study instead aimed to identify the most effective content of pictorial health warning labels and whether educational attainment moderates those effects.

In field experiments, 529 adult smokers and 530 young adults (258 nonsmokers; 271 smokers) reported their responses to different pictorial health warning labels printed on cigarette packages; one experiment manipulated textual form (testimonial narrative vs. didactic) and the other manipulated image type (diseased organs vs. human suffering).

Mean ratings and rankings showed that pictorial health warning labels with didactic textual forms had equivalent or significantly higher credibility, relevance, and impact than labels with testimonial forms, and mixed-effects models confirmed these results.

Responses differed by participant educational attainment: didactic forms were consistently rated higher than testimonials among participants with higher education, whereas the difference between didactic and testimonial narrative forms was weaker or not statistically significant among participants with lower education.

Because the reported outcome was participants' self-reported responses to different pictorial health warning labels rather than smoking behavior or health outcomes, this experimental design cannot establish that pictorial warning labels reduce smoking-related health disparities across education or socioeconomic groups.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: reduction in smoking-related health disparities in smoking behavior or health outcomes across education or socioeconomic groups.

The retrieved evidence is insufficient to establish whether prophylactic antibiotics are necessary for totally implantable venous access device (TIVAD) placement by interventional radiologists, because no comparative infection outcome between patients who did and did not receive prophylactic antibiotics is reported; the available single-study data show that CLABSIs occurred in seven of 1,183 (0.6%) patients within 30 days of placement, in a series whose stated aim was to determine the early infection rate for TIVADs placed without antibiotic prophylaxis.

In that series, 1,183 ports were placed and 13 were removed; at the time of TIVAD placement, 81 (7%) patients were receiving antibiotics incidental to the procedure, and one patient who received an antibiotic on the day of implantation developed a CLABSI.

These figures come from a retrospective chart review that cross-referenced a list of patients who underwent TIVAD placement in 2009 with all TIVAD removals from January 1, 2009, through January 30, 2010, in order to identify devices removed within 30 days of placement; such a single-cohort, retrospective design can describe early infection rates in devices placed without routine prophylaxis but cannot by itself establish whether prophylactic antibiotics change infection outcomes, because no prophylaxis versus no-prophylaxis comparison is reported.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: comparative infection outcomes between antibiotic prophylaxis and no prophylaxis.

Yes: in a pilot manikin study, a four-diagram instruction manual with speech bubbles enabled laypersons to operate the Laryngeal Mask Supreme® (LMAS), with 145 of 150 participants (96.7%) inserting the device into the manikin in the right direction.
The intervention tested was an instruction manual of four illustrations with speech bubbles displaying the correct use of the LMAS.

Laypersons were handed a bag containing an LMAS, a bag mask valve device (BMV), a syringe prefilled with air and the instruction sheet, and were asked to perform and ventilate the manikin as displayed; time to ventilation was recorded and degree of success evaluated.
The device was inserted inverted or twisted in 13 (8.7%) attempts, and eight (5.3%) individuals recognized this and corrected the position.

Within the first 2 minutes, 119 (79.3%) applicants were able to insert the LMAS and provide tidal volumes greater than 150 ml (estimated dead space), and time to insertion and first ventilation was 83.2 ± 29 s.

Because this was a pilot study of laypersons using a manikin, the reported insertion and ventilation success rates describe simulated performance and do not by themselves establish successful device use in actual patients.

Ioflupane, N-u-fluoropropyl-2a-carbomethoxy-3a-(4-iodophenyl) nortropane, also called FP-CIT, labelled with (123)I (commercially known as DaTSCAN) has been proven to be useful in the differential diagnosis between PD and ET and to confirm dopaminergic degeneration in patients with parkinsonism. the authors used DaTSCAN to obtain SPECT images and measure the radiopharmaceutical uptake in the striatum (S), as well as the caudate nucleus (CN) and putamen (P) in all individuals.
Twenty-eight patients suffering from ET (10 males plus 18 females) and 28 NV (12 males and 16 females) were enroled in this study.

In addition, 33 patients (11 males and 22 females) with an established diagnosis of PD with unilateral limb involvement (12 left hemi-body and 21 right hemi-body) were included for comparison with ET.
Qualitative (Visual) interpretation of the SPECT data did not find any difference in the uptake of the radiopharmaceutical at the level of the S, CN and P between NV and ET patients.
Semiquantitative analysis revealed significant differences between NV and ET patients in the striatum, reduced in the latter.

In this study DaTSCAN SPECT separated PD from ET: reduced accumulation of the radiopharmaceutical uptake was found in the putamen of all PD patients, there was a significant reduction in tracer accumulation in the left putamen of patients with right hemi-parkinsonism compared with ET and NV, and patients with left hemi-parkinsonism showed reduced radioligand uptake in the right putamen in comparison with ET and NV.

Clinical follow-up of 20 patients with ET (interval not specified in the source) revealed no significant change in clinical presentation, particularly no signs of PD, and follow-up DaTSCAN performed in 10 of them was negative in all but one, that single patient having had an equivocal baseline study which deteriorated 12 months later.

In the Dutch Surgical Colorectal Audit database, all available process indicators for surgical colorectal cancer care were aggregated into five different composite measures, and consistency between these composite process measures and outcome indicators was examined longitudinally for 85 Dutch hospitals.
The analyses included 4732 elective patients with colon carcinoma and 2239 with rectum carcinoma, all treated in the 85 hospitals studied.
The association between each composite measure and risk-adjusted postoperative mortality and morbidity was analysed at both the patient and the hospital level.
At the patient level, only one of the composite measures was negatively associated with morbidity for rectum carcinoma.

At the hospital level, a strong negative association was found between the composite measures and hospital mortality and morbidity rates for rectum carcinoma (p<0.05), and with hospital morbidity rates for colon carcinoma.

PMID:22497340 was designed to clarify whether horizontal canal ocular reflex is influenced by otolith organs input; the subjects were seven healthy humans, the right ear was stimulated using ice-water, nystagmus was analysed using three-dimensional video-oculography, and each subject was kept in a left-ear-down position for 20 s and then repositioned to a prone position, a right-ear-down position and a supine position with 20 s intervals.

In that study, eye movements in the supine position and the prone position were not in a symmetric fashion, and nystagmus in the left-ear-down position and the right-ear-down position were not symmetric either; the authors state that these phenomena indicate that the axis of the eyeball rotation was affected by the shift of the direction of gravity exerted on the head.

Because the study varied head orientation relative to gravity in seven healthy humans rather than directly stimulating or abolishing otolith organ function, the findings support an association between the direction of gravity acting on the head and the axis of eye rotation rather than isolating a causal otolith contribution.
The study was performed to evaluate the clinical and technical efficacy of endovenous laser ablation (EVLA) of small saphenous varicosities, particularly in relation to the site of endovenous access.
Totally 59 patients with unilateral saphenopopliteal junction incompetence and small saphenous vein reflux underwent EVLA (810 nm, 14 W diode laser) with ambulatory phlebectomies.
Small saphenous vein access was gained at the lowest site of truncal reflux.
Patients were divided into 2 groups: access gained above mid-calf (AMC, n = 33) and below mid-calf (BMC, n = 26) levels.
Both groups demonstrated significant improvement in VCSS, AVVQ, generic quality of life Short Form 36, and EuroQol scores (P<.05) up to 1 year.

No differences were seen between AMC and BMC groups for complications (phlebitis: 2 [6%] and 1 [3.8%], P>.05; paresthesia: 2 [6%] and 5 [19%], P =.223) and recurrence (3 [9%] and 1 [3.8%], P =.623), respectively.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: between-group differences in VCSS, AVVQ, and patient satisfaction by access site.

The cited evidence does not support a uniform conclusion that Indigenous Australians age prematurely compared with other Australians: although some conditions are highly prevalent from middle age onwards, Indigenous life expectancy matched that of non-Indigenous people 7 years older, and there was no consistent 20-year lead in age-specific prevalence of age-associated conditions.

Analysis of life tables for Indigenous and non-Indigenous populations showed that at age 63 for women and age 65 for men, Indigenous people had the same life expectancy as non-Indigenous people at age 70 — an approximately 7-year, not 20-year, difference at those ages.

A cross-sectional analysis of aged care assessment, hospital and health survey data comparing Indigenous and non-Indigenous age-specific prevalence of health conditions found no consistent pattern of a 20-year lead in age-specific prevalence of age-associated conditions for Indigenous compared with other Australians.
That analysis reported high prevalence from middle-age onwards of some conditions, particularly diabetes (type unspecified), but little or no lead for others.

Because the prevalence comparison was cross-sectional, it describes age-specific prevalence at a point in time and cannot by itself establish that Indigenous Australians experience an accelerated aging process.

In obese patients with Type 2 diabetes and no clinical features of Cushing's syndrome, late-night salivary cortisol was not a better screening test than 24-hour urinary free cortisol on specificity: its specificity was significantly lower than that of 24hr UFC (P=0.039), while it did not differ significantly from the 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test (P>0.99).

The reported specificities were 70% (95% CI 53-83%) for late-night salivary cortisol at a cutoff of 10 nmol/L, 90% (95% CI 76-97%) for 24hr UFC at 400 nmol, and 72% (95% CI 55-85%) for the 1 mg DST at 50 nmol/L.

The specificities of the three tests using various cutoffs were calculated and compared under the assumption that none of the 40 recruited obese patients with Type 2 diabetes had hypercortisolism; all 40 provided late-night salivary cortisol samples, 38 completed all three tests, and two completed only two screening tests.

Because the analysis assumed that no patient had hypercortisolism, the comparison between late-night salivary cortisol and the standard tests rests on specificity rather than on detecting cortisol excess, so the study does not establish comparative sensitivity or overall diagnostic accuracy for detecting cortisol excess.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: comparative sensitivity or overall diagnostic accuracy for detecting cortisol excess.

Resection of SLM and CRC can be undertaken at different centres (separate management, SM) or at the same centre (global management, GM); a retrospective study of SLM and CRC resections carried out during 01/2000 - 12/2006 by SM or GM, using a combined or delayed strategy, compared these approaches.

Among patients whose liver resection was delayed (62 SM, 17 GM), chemotherapy before liver surgery was given to 92% of SM versus 38% of GM patients (P<0.0001), and the median delay between the two procedures was 212 days for SM versus 182 days for GM (P = 0.04); the first step of liver resection was performed during colorectal surgery in 62% of GM versus 6% of SM patients (P<0.0001), and the mean number of procedures (CRC+SLM) was lower in GM at 1.6 versus 2.3 in SM (P = 0.003).
Three-month mortality was 3% in the GM group and 0% in the SM group, a difference that was not statistically significant.
Overall survival was 67% for SM versus 51% for GM at 3 years and 35% versus 31% at 5 years, with neither comparison statistically significant.
Disease-free survival to 5 years was higher in SM patients than in GM patients (14% vs.

In young obese males, mean common carotid artery pulsatility index and resistance index were statistically higher than in healthy controls; these indexes were calculated from blood flow velocity curves obtained by pulsed Doppler ultrasonography in 35 young obese males and 23 age-matched healthy male volunteers.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Early signs of vascular abnormalities.

In Hirschsprung's disease, the radiographic transition zone on contrast enema was concordant with the level of aganglionosis on the pathology specimen in 8 of 19 rectal-form cases (42%), 20 of 35 rectosigmoid-form cases (57%), all 6 long-segment cases (100%), and both (2) total colonic form cases (100%), with a global agreement of 58.1%, κ = 0.39, CI [0.24; 0.57].

From 1998 to 2009, 79 patients were operated on for Hirschsprung's disease; all available preoperative contrast enemas (n = 61) had been single blind reviewed by the same radiologist, who defined the radiographic transition zone when present in vertebral level.

Four groups were determined (rectal, rectosigmoid, long segment, and absence of transition zone) and by Kappa coefficient of agreement correlated to the length of aganglionosis in the pathological report.
The aim of the study was to analyse this correlation more precisely to improve preoperative planning of the corrective surgery.

This study establishes the degree of agreement between the radiographic transition zone and the level of aganglionosis on the pathology specimen but does not by itself establish that using the radiographic transition zone to plan corrective surgery improves surgical outcomes.

Micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) appears reliable for assessing the microstructure of the maxillary alveolar bone at the alveolar process, based on direct comparison with conventional stereologic-based histomorphometry showing significant positive correlations between micro-CT bone volumetric density (BV/TV) and histologic percentage of bone.

In that study, osseous microstructural variables including BV/TV were analyzed by micro-CT in 39 biopsies from the maxillary alveolar bone, whereas conventional stereologic-based histomorphometry was performed on 10 bone biopsies using optic microscopy (OM) and low-vacuum surface electronic microscopy (SEM), and the percentages of bone obtained by the two approaches were compared.

Significant positive correlations were observed between micro-CT BV/TV and the percentage of bone (%Bone) analyzed by SEM (r = 0.933, P < 0.001), by toluidine blue staining OM (r = 0.950, P < 0.001), and by dark field OM (r = 0.667, P = 0.05).

The study also reported a high positive correlation between BV/TV and trabecular thickness, such that a BV/TV value above 50% corresponded to bone in which most trabeculae were thicker than 0.2 mm, and a high negative correlation between BV/TV and trabecular separation, such that BV/TV above 50% corresponded to most trabeculae being separated by less than 0.3 mm.

Acceptance of the Danish national preventive home visit programme for older people was socially imbalanced: among 1,023 community-dwelling 80-year-olds, those with high financial assets accepted preventive home visits more frequently than those with low assets (adjusted OR = 1.5, 95% CI 1.1-2.0), with acceptance ascertained by questionnaire, financial assets taken from national registry data, and logistic regression analyses adjusted for gender.
The association between financial assets and acceptance of preventive home visits was attenuated when the analysis was adjusted for the municipalities' invitational procedures.

The odds ratio for accepting preventive home visits was larger among persons with low financial assets who were invited by a letter with a proposed date than among persons with high financial assets invited by other procedures, although these estimates had wide confidence intervals.

Consenting eligible adults (N=238) from 18-100 years of age consecutively admitted to inpatient psychiatry units were assessed using the SCID I and II, the Coping Orientations to Problems Experienced Scale (COPE), the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS), the Global Assessment of Functioning Scale (GAF), the Social and Occupational Functioning Assessment Scale (SOFAS), the 12 Item Short-Form Heath Survey (SF12), the Sarason Social Support Questionnaire, and the NEO Five Factor Inventory (NEO-FFI) (cognitively impaired, and non-English speaking patients were excluded).

Personality traits, social supports, gender, and age predicted coping strategies, while Axis I diagnosis, education, personality disorder, and symptom severity were not significant predictors of coping strategies.
As assessed by the COPE, older adults reported lower levels of dysfunctional coping strategies than younger adults.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: an age × personality disorder interaction (moderation) effect on coping style in psychiatric inpatients.
To evaluate retrospectively whether technical factors of hepatic arterial embolization affect the prognosis of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

Inclusion criteria of this study were the following: (1) patients received embolization as the initial treatment during 2003-2004, (2) Child A or B liver profile, (3) five or fewer HCCs with maximum diameter of 7 cm or smaller, and (4) no extrahepatic metastasis.
Patient data were gathered from 43 centers.
Eight hundred fifteen patients were enrolled.
Prognostic factors were evaluated using univariate and multivariate analyses.

Univariate analysis showed a Child-Pugh class-A, alpha-fetoprotein level lower than 100 ng/ml, tumor size of 3 cm or smaller, tumor number of 3 or fewer, one-lobe tumor distribution, nodular tumor type, within the Milan criteria, stage I or II, no portal venous invasion, use of iodized oil, and selective embolization were significantly better prognostic factors.
In the multivariate Cox model, the benefit to survival of selective embolization remained significant (hazard ratio 0.68; 95 % CI 0.48-0.97; p = 0.033).

Because the prognostic evaluation was performed retrospectively, the reported association between selective embolization and better survival cannot by itself establish that the technique causes improved outcomes.

Ultrasound retains a role in the assessment of internal derangements of the temporomandibular joint, but with acknowledged limitations: imaging by static and dynamic high-resolution ultrasound demonstrated considerably lower sensitivity compared with magnetic resonance, and the presence of articular sounds and physical signs was often insufficient to detect disk displacement.

In this diagnostic study, 40 patients and 20 asymptomatic volunteers (120 temporomandibular joints) underwent a standardized interview, physical examination, and static and dynamic articular ultrasound, with sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values calculated against magnetic resonance as the reference test.
The authors reported that some of the technical difficulties of the ultrasound examination resulted from limited access because of the presence of surrounding bone structures.

Yes — third trimester sonography predicted the presentation of the first twin (twin A) at delivery in a retrospective cohort of 238 twin pregnancies evaluated from 2007 to 2009 (896 ultrasounds reviewed): the positive predictive value of a cephalic presentation of twin A on ultrasound for persistence of cephalic presentation at delivery reached 95% after 28 weeks' gestation, and the positive predictive value of a sonographically established noncephalic presentation for noncephalic presentation at delivery was greater than 90% after 32 weeks' gestation.

Because this was a retrospective review of sonogram records at seven gestational age intervals and of inpatient medical records, with positive predictive value, sensitivity and specificity calculated for each interval, it reports the predictive value of sonographic presentation at given gestational ages rather than demonstrating that acting on the ultrasound finding changes delivery outcomes.

No: in a controlled feeding analysis, African American women did not require fewer calories than non-African American women to maintain stable weight — during intervention feeding their mean (SD) intake was 2168 (293) kcal versus 2073 (284) kcal, i.e.
94.7 kcal higher (P<.05), and after adjustment for potential confounders there was no difference in caloric intake (Δ = -2.8 kcal, P =.95).

The analysis included 206 women (73% African American), aged 22-75 years, who participated in the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) trial, a multicenter, randomized, controlled feeding study comparing 3 dietary patterns on blood pressure in individuals with prehypertension or stage 1 hypertension, and calorie intake was adjusted during feeding to maintain stable weight.
At baseline, African American women had higher weight and body mass index than non-African American women (78.4 vs 72.4 kg, P<.01; 29.0 vs 27.6 kg/m(2), P<.05, respectively).

A training model for retroperitoneoscopic nephrectomy (RPN) exists and was developed experimentally in a porcine (piglet) model, in which fifteen piglets were operated on and fifteen RPNs were performed, all with three ports.
The authors report that RPN in a porcine model could simulate the whole procedure, from creating the retroperitoneal space to nephrectomy completion.

After statistical data analysis, the experimental learning curve for the porcine RPN training model was eight cases; animals were divided into group A (the first eight cases) and group B (the last seven cases), with statistically significant differences between the groups in peritoneal opening (p = 0.025), operative time (p = 0.0037) and blood loss (p = 0.026).

In these fifteen porcine RPNs, operative time ranged from 15 to 50 minutes (median 30 minutes) and blood loss ranged from 5 to 100 mL (median 20 mL), with five peritoneal openings and two surgical vascular complications managed laparoscopically.
The evidence for this model comes from an experimental animal (piglet) study, so it supports the feasibility of a training model rather than clinical outcomes in patients.

For articles published in the intensive care medicine journal Intensive Care Medicine in 2008, the retrieved evidence on whether open access publishing increases impact is mixed: the median number of citations was 8 (interquartile range 4-12) for non-open access articles versus 9 (6-18) for open access articles, a difference that was not statistically significant (p=0.084).
Among the most-cited articles (citation range >8), the citation count was 13 (10-16) for non-open access articles and 18 (13-21) for open access articles (p=0.008).
In the 30-35 months after publication, the average number of citations per article per month was 0.28 ± 0.6 for non-open access articles versus 0.38 ± 0.7 for open access articles (p=0.043).

In a linear multiple regression model adjusting for potentially confounding variables, independent factors for citation advantage were the Hirsch index of the first signing author (β=0.207; p=0.015) and open access status (β=3.618; p=0.006).
The analysis evaluated 161 articles, 76% of which were non-open access, published in Intensive Care Medicine in 2008, with citation data compared between the two groups up until April 30, 2011.

Because this evidence comes from a single discipline — intensive care medicine — and from one journal's 2008 output, it cannot establish that open access publishing increases the impact of scientific articles generally, and the relationship between open access and citation counts in intensive care medicine had not been studied previously.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: general impact across scientific articles outside intensive care medicine.

In a study of 60 middle-aged individuals without diabetes, both fasting and 2-hour plasma glucose were associated with a higher Framingham risk score (fasting glucose r² = 0.21; 2-hour glucose r² = 0.24; P<0.001 for both), while insulin sensitivity was associated with a lower Framingham risk score (r² = 0.36; P<0.001), a pattern consistent with insulin resistance explaining the glucose–cardiovascular risk link.

Adjustment for insulin sensitivity and 2-hour glucose rendered the effect of fasting glucose on Framingham risk score non-significant (P = 0.060), and adjusting for insulin sensitivity and fasting glucose made the association between 2-hour glucose and Framingham risk score disappear (P = 0.143).

In contrast, insulin sensitivity remained associated with Framingham risk score after adjustment for glucose levels (P<0.001), indicating that in this cohort the glucose–Framingham risk score associations were attributable to underlying insulin sensitivity rather than glucose itself.

This evidence comes from cross-sectional linear regression modelling of associations in 60 non-diabetic participants, so it can show that the glucose associations did not persist after accounting for insulin sensitivity but cannot by itself establish that insulin resistance causally drives cardiovascular risk.

In a single-center retrospective cohort review of 308 patients who underwent surgery for hip fracture between September 2006 and December 2008, of whom 73 received regional anesthesia and 235 received general anesthesia, rates of readmission were not statistically different between the two anesthesia groups.

Because the comparison was retrospective and historical, with regional anesthesia used mainly after July 2007 and general anesthesia mainly before July 2007, this design cannot establish that regional anesthesia causes a difference or absence of difference in postoperative outcomes.
In-hospital mortality was not statistically different between the regional and general anesthesia groups in this geriatric hip fracture cohort.

The average cost of hospitalization, estimated from hospital charges, did not differ between patients who received regional versus general anesthesia for hip fracture surgery ($16,789 ± 631 vs $16,815 ± 643, respectively; P = 0.9557).
The retrieved evidence does not establish: postoperative morbidity/complication rates between regional and general anesthesia groups.

Vitamin D deficiency was not a distinguishing feature of pediatric celiac disease in the cited retrospective comparison: prepubertal children aged 3-12 years with untreated celiac disease (n=24) and prepubertal non-celiac children of the same age (n=50) had no significant difference in serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] level (27.58 +/- 9.91 versus 26.20 +/- 10.45, p = 0.59).

In the same study, when patients were subdivided into obese and non-obese groups, non-obese celiac patients and non-obese normal children did not differ in 25(OH)D level (28.39 +/- 10.26 versus 30.64 +/- 12.08, p = 0.52), whereas non-obese celiac patients had a significantly higher 25(OH)D level than the obese normal children (28.39 +/- 10.26 versus 21.58 +/- 5.67, p = 0.009); the season of 25(OH)D measurement was not a significant confounder (p = 0.7).

The comparison was retrospective and included children diagnosed with celiac disease by intestinal biopsy who were not on a gluten-free diet, with exclusion of children having diseases of calcium or vitamin D metabolism or receiving calcium or vitamin D supplementation, so the design supports an association between untreated celiac disease and vitamin D status at the time of measurement rather than any causal or longitudinal effect.

The Prospective Urban Rural Epidemiology study in the North West Province, South Africa, started in 2005 and included African volunteers (n = 1994; aged>30 years) from a sample of 6000 randomly selected households in rural and urban areas; it explored health behaviours and conventional risk factors of African individuals with optimal blood pressure (BP) (≤ 120/80 mm Hg) and their 5-year prediction for the development of hypertension.
Those with optimal BP (n = 478) were followed at a success rate of 70% for 5 years (213 normotensive, 68 hypertensive, 57 deceased).

Africans that became hypertensive smoked more than the normotensive individuals (68.2% vs 49.8%), and they also had a greater waist circumference [ratio of geometric means of 0.94 cm (95% CI: 0.86-0.99)] and greater amount of γ-glutamyltransferase [0.74 U/l (95% CI: 0.62-0.88)] at baseline.
Alcohol intake also predicted central systolic BP and carotid cross-sectional wall area (CSWA) at follow-up.
The 5-year change in BP was independently explained by baseline γ-glutamyltransferase [R(2) = 0.23, β = 0.13 U/l (95% CI: 0.01-0.19)].
Waist circumference was another predictor of BP changes [β = 0.18 cm (95% CI: 0.05-0.24)] and CSWA.

Because these results come from a prospective observational cohort that reports baseline risk-factor differences between those who did and did not become hypertensive and predictors of 5-year BP change, they describe associations and do not establish that behavioural risk factors are responsible for the conversion from optimal blood pressure to hypertensive status.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: causal evidence that behavioural risk factors are responsible for conversion from optimal blood pressure to hypertensive status.

Stress did not increase imitation of drinking behavior: in a 2 (confederate's drinking condition: alcohol vs. soda) × 2 (participant's stress condition: stress vs. no stress) experiment in which 106 young male adults were randomly assigned to conditions and, directly after the stress or no-stress period, confederates and participants entered a bar laboratory where their drinking behavior was observed, participants in both the stress and no-stress conditions consumed substantially more alcohol when confederates drank alcohol than when they drank soda, while there was no difference in alcohol consumed between the stress and no-stress conditions and no moderating effect of stress on the tendency to drink along with peers was found.

In a single-center retrospective cohort of 2329 singleton term live births from 2009-2010, 50.2% of women had an ultrasound-obtained estimated fetal weight (US-EFW) within 1 month of delivery, and cesarean delivery (CD) was significantly more common among women with US-EFW than among those without (15.7% vs 10.2%; P<.001).

After adjustment for potential confounders, US-EFW within 1 month of delivery remained an independent risk factor for CD (odds ratio, 1.44; 95% confidence interval, 1.1-1.9), and the risk was higher when US-EFW exceeded 3500 g (odds ratio, 1.8; 95% confidence interval, 1.3-2.7).
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Effect of modifying ultrasound-estimated fetal weight knowledge or use on cesarean delivery rate.

The cited evidence links cigarette tax increases to retail prices by showing that in China the 2009 excise tax increase on cigarettes did not translate into higher retail prices, because the Chinese State Tobacco Monopoly Administration (STMA) used its policy authority to ensure that retail cigarette prices did not change.

In China the government tax increase was collected at both the producer and wholesale levels, and as a result the 2009 excise tax increase produced higher tax revenue for the government and lower profits for the tobacco industry, with no increase in the retail price of cigarettes for consumers.

In Korea, cigarette excise taxes and the price of a typical pack of cigarettes have not increased since 2005, and both the effective tax rate as a fraction of price and the real price of cigarettes have been falling.

In a retrospective analysis of patients in an academic breast service who underwent mastectomy with or without reconstruction and received adjuvant chemotherapy, immediate breast reconstruction (IBR) did not compromise delivery of adjuvant chemotherapy: there was no significant difference in the median time to chemotherapy between groups.
The comparison was made between 107 patients who received IBR and 113 patients who received mastectomy alone.
Overall complication rates were comparable between the groups (mastectomy alone 45.1% versus IBR 35.5%, p = 0.2).
There was more return to surgery in the IBR group, with 11.5% of tissue expanders requiring removal, whilst more seromas occurred in the mastectomy group.

Because the study was a retrospective analysis, the absence of a difference in chemotherapy timing describes an association observed in the recorded data rather than establishing that performing IBR preserves chemotherapy delivery.
It has been reported that individuals with type 1 diabetes consume a high atherogenic diet.

In the EURODIAB Prospective Complications Study, 1102 patients with type 1 diabetes (553 men, 549 women, baseline age 33 ± 10 years, diabetes duration 15 ± 9 years) had complete nutritional data at baseline and after 7 years.

At the 7-year follow-up, reported protein (-0.35% energy (en)), fat (-1.07% en), saturated fat (-0.25% en) and cholesterol (-7.42 mg/1000 kcal) intakes were lower, while carbohydrate (+1.23% en) and fibre (+0.46 g/1000 kcal) intakes were higher, representing minor changes from baseline.

European recommendations for adequate nutrient intakes were followed for protein by 76% at baseline and 78% at follow-up, moderately for fat (34%, 40%), carbohydrate (34%, 41%) and cholesterol (39%, 47%), but poorly for fibre (1.4%, 2.4%) and saturated fat (11%, 13%).

In 94 HIV-infected patients with a normal clinical cardiovascular examination, gated myocardial perfusion SPECT detected coronary artery disease in nine patients (eight with ischaemia and one with myocardial infarction), corresponding to a 9.6 % positivity rate.
All but two of the scintigraphic diagnoses of ischaemia were confirmed by coronarography.

Univariate analysis showed that the overall number of cardiovascular risk factors and the combination of gender and age were associated with a diagnosis of silent myocardial ischaemia (p<0.05), while multivariate analysis identified the combination of gender and age as the only independent parameter significantly associated with the scintigraphic diagnosis (p = 0.01).

All positive myocardial SPECT scans occurred in men older than 52 years with at least two other cardiovascular risk factors, and within that subpopulation of 47 patients the prevalence of silent myocardial ischaemia detected by SPECT reached 19.2 %.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Evidence that screening with gated myocardial perfusion SPECT improves clinical outcomes or an explicit recommendation for its use in HIV-infected patients.

Yes — in the 1993 Pelotas birth cohort, obesity at the start of adolescence was a risk factor for wheezing: the prevalence of wheezing at 15 years was 50% greater among individuals who were obese at 11 years than among those who were eutrophic at 11 years (RR 1.53; 95% CI: 1.14-2.05), independent of the effect of various confounding variables.
After controlling for confounding factors, the risk of persistent wheezing among individuals who were obese at 11 years was 1.82 (95% CI: 1.30-2.54).
The greater the skinfold tertile at 11 years, the higher the prevalence of wheezing at 15 years was (p =.011).
Weight status and skinfolds did not present any association with incident wheezing.

Yes — the Townsville Cancer Centre audit reported that intensive chemotherapy regimens given to rural patients with node-positive breast and metastatic colorectal cancers at the same doses as urban patients was safe in practice, with no toxic death in either group and only two patients transferred to Townsville for admission.

The assessment was a retrospective audit of patients with metastatic colorectal and node-positive breast cancers during a 24-month period, in which rurality was determined by the rural, remote and metropolitan classification and Fisher's exact test was used for analysis.

Of the 121 patients included, 70 had breast cancer and 51 had colon cancer; the urban versus rural split was 68 versus 53 among all patients, 43 versus 27 in the breast cancer subgroup and 25 versus 26 in the colorectal cancer subgroup.
A total of 421 cycles was given, with dose intensity of more than 95% for breast cancer in both the urban and rural groups (P>0.05).
The rate of febrile neutropenia was 9.3% versus 7.4% between the compared groups (P = 0.56).
For XELOX, the rate of diarrhoea was 20% versus 19% (P = 0.66) and the rate of vomiting was 20% versus 11% (P = 0.11) between the compared groups.
Side-effects were usually managed locally by rural general practitioners.

As a retrospective audit that compared observed serious adverse event profiles and dose intensities, the design cannot establish that rural administration of intensive chemotherapy causes safety equivalent to urban administration; it documents that the audited records showed no toxic deaths and comparable adverse-event rates.

The retrieved evidence is insufficient to establish whether etoricoxib prevents heterotopic ossification after primary total hip arthroplasty relative to placebo or another NSAID, because the only identified study was a single-arm prospective two-stage phase-2 design in a small sample (n = 42) that reported outcomes only for patients who took etoricoxib.

In that study, oral etoricoxib 90 mg was given for seven days to patients who received a cemented primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis, and heterotopic ossification was determined six months after surgery on anteroposterior pelvic radiographs using the Brooker classification.
Among the patients who took etoricoxib, no heterotopic ossification was found in 62%, while 31% had Brooker grade 1 and 7% had Brooker grade 2 ossification.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: comparative effectiveness versus placebo or another NSAID.

Yes — the type of tibial component affected postoperative mechanical alignment after unicompartmental knee replacement: in a retrospective review of 89 patients who underwent robotic-guided UKR, mean postoperative mechanical alignment was significantly closer to neutral in the Onlay group (metal-backed onlay component; mean=2.8°; 95% CI=2.4°, 3.2°) than in the Inlay group (all-polyethylene inlay component; mean=3.9°; 95% CI=3.4°, 4.4°).
The between-group alignment difference was reported with R2=0.65 and P=0.003, after adjusting for gender, BMI, age, side and preoperative mechanical alignment.
In the same cohort, the thickness of the tibial polyethylene insert also had a significant effect on postoperative alignment when added to the model (R2=0.68; P=0.01).

Because the evidence comes from a retrospective review of patients treated with robotic guidance, it shows an association between tibial component type and postoperative mechanical alignment and cannot by itself establish that selecting one component type causes a different alignment.

In a single-institution series of 49 epithelial ovarian cancer patients (median age 57 years, range 28-76) undergoing quaternary cytoreduction for relapse a median of 16 months (range 2-142 months) after previous chemotherapy, the median duration of surgery was 292 min.

Major operative morbidity after quaternary cytoreduction was 28.6% and 30-day mortality was 2%; mean overall survival was 23.05 months (95% CI 15.5-30.6) over a mean follow-up of 18.41 months (95% CI 12.64-24.18).

The study was designed to evaluate surgical outcome and survival benefit after quaternary cytoreduction in epithelial ovarian cancer relapse, and it systematically evaluated all consecutive patients undergoing quaternary cytoreduction at one institution over a 12-year period (October 2000 to January 2012).

In this cohort, surgical effort still mattered: mean overall survival was 43 months (95% CI 26.4-59.5) for patients with no tumour residuals versus 13.4 months (95% CI 7.42-19.4) for patients with any tumour residuals (P=0.001).
Mean overall survival was 40.5 months (95% CI 27.4-53.6) for the 18 patients (36.7%) who received postoperative chemotherapy versus 12.03 months (95% CI 5.9-18.18) for those who did not (P<0.001).

Multivariate analysis identified multifocal tumour dissemination as predictive of incomplete tumour resection, higher operative morbidity and lower survival, while systemic chemotherapy after quaternary cytoreduction had a protective, statistically significant impact on overall survival; ascites, platinum resistance, high grading and advanced age had no prognostic impact.

Because these findings come from a retrospective consecutive single-institution series of 49 patients rather than a randomised comparison, the reported survival differences by residual tumour and by postoperative chemotherapy are associations and cannot establish that intensifying surgical effort or giving chemotherapy causes the longer survival.

The retrieved evidence is insufficient to establish that early second-look tympanoplasty reduces the rate of conversion to modified radical mastoidectomy, because the cited series reports conversion outcomes without a no-second-look or alternative-management comparator.

In a single-surgeon retrospective review of 132 second-look operations performed between 2006 and 2012 (mean interval from primary surgery to second look 6 months), most recurrent and residual cholesteatoma was easily removed at second look (73.1%), only 4 cases were converted to a modified radical mastoidectomy (3%), and 3 cases required a third-look procedure.

The design of this study — a retrospective, single-surgeon case series — entails that it can report the observed conversion rate after planned second-look surgery but cannot by itself show that early second-look tympanoplasty lowers conversion to modified radical mastoidectomy relative to another strategy.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: comparative reduction in conversion to modified radical mastoidectomy versus no early second-look or another management strategy.

Whether an HIV-1/2 point-of-care test on sputum will work for screening TB/HIV co-infection in Central India is only partly answered: the cited cross-sectional study reports that the OraQuick® HIV-1/2 Assay on sputum agreed closely with serum ELISA in patients diagnosed with tuberculosis, but the retrieved evidence does not establish diagnostic performance specifically in Central India.

In that cross-sectional study, sputa from patients diagnosed with tuberculosis were tested for antibodies to HIV with the OraQuick® HIV-1/2 Assay (OraSure Technologies, Inc., Bethlehem, PA, USA), and the results were compared with those of serum ELISA.

Compared with serum ELISA, the OraQuick® HIV-1/2 Assay in sputum specimens reported 90% sensitivity (9/10) and 100% specificity (307/307), with a positive predictive value of 100% (95%CI: 66.37%-100.00%) and a negative predictive value of 99.68% (95%CI: 98.20%-99.99%).

Because the reported evidence comes from a cross-sectional comparison of sputum OraQuick® against serum ELISA, it cannot by itself establish how the assay performs in a screening programme over time or in the specific setting of Central India.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Diagnostic performance specifically in Central India.
The source systematic review and meta-analysis was designed to compare the clinical effectiveness of operative with nonoperative treatment for displaced midshaft clavicular fractures (DMCF).

The authors systematically searched electronic databases (MEDILINE, EMBASE, CLINICAL, OVID, BIOSIS and Cochrane registry of controlled clinical trials) to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in which operative treatment was compared with nonoperative treatment for DMCF from 1980 to 2012.
Four RCTs with a total of 321 patients were screened for the present study.

Results showed that the operative treatment was superior to the nonoperative treatment regarding the rate of nonunion [95 % confidence interval (CI) (0.05, 0.43), P = 0.0004], malunion [95 % CI (0.06, 0.34), P < 0.00001] and overall complication [95 % CI (0.43-0.76), P = 0.0001].

Subgroup analyses of complications revealed that significant differences were existed in the incidence of neurologic symptoms [95 % CI (0.20, 0.74), P = 0.004] and dissatisfaction with appearance [95 % CI (0.19, 0.65), P = 0.001].
Lack of consistent and standardized assessment data, insufficiency analysis that carried out showed improved functional outcomes (P < 0.05) in operative treatment.

The reported improvement in functional outcomes with operative treatment was derived from an analysis carried out in the setting of a lack of consistent and standardized assessment data, so that functional-outcome result rests on incomplete and non-standardized assessment.

The so-called "globulomaxillary cyst", previously described as a fissural cyst caused by entrapped epithelium between the nasal and maxillary process, is no longer considered an entity of its own, although cystic lesions corresponding to the former image of globulomaxillary cysts still occur in daily practice.

In a retrospective study, 17 cases (12 men and 5 women, 12-59 years old) of primarily diagnosed globulomaxillary cysts were analysed according to clinical, radiological and histological aspects, catamnestically processed and assigned to a new entity.

Reclassification of those 17 lesions yielded seven lateral periodontal cysts, four radicular cysts, two keratocystic odontogenic tumours, one adenomatoid odontogenic tumour, one periapical granuloma, one residual cyst and one undefined jaw cyst.

Yes: in a longitudinal, retrospective cohort of community-dwelling older adults aged 65 years or older in a Michigan home- and community-based waiver program, a fall occurred at a rate of 33% among the 862 older adults with cancer versus 29% among the 8,617 older adults without cancer (p<0.00), with falls reported over 90-180 days.
Older adults with a history of cancer were more likely to fall than those without cancer, with an adjusted odds ratio of 1.16 (95% confidence interval 1.02, 1.33; p = 0.03).
No differences in fall rates were determined by cancer type or stage, and the odds of a fall did not increase when time since cancer diagnosis was added.

Because the evidence comes from an observational, retrospective cohort design, the reported higher odds of falling among older adults with a history of cancer indicate an association rather than a causal effect of cancer on falls.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: worldwide/multicenter confirmation that vancomycin MIC creep is a global phenomenon.
In six group interviews with 17 patients with knee OA, the idea of using colour to describe OA pain was generally acceptable, but it did not suit all participants as a way of describing their pain.

The majority of these participants chose red to describe high-intensity pain, citing associations with inflammation, fire, anger and the stop signal in a traffic light system, while a range of colours was chosen to represent changes in pain intensity.
Colours chosen to describe the absence of pain were selected for their association with positive emotional feelings such as purity, calmness and happiness.
Aching pain was consistently associated with colours such as grey or black, whereas sharp pain was described using a wider selection of colours.

The majority of the 17 patients with knee OA thought they would be able to use colour to describe their pain to healthcare professionals, although issues around the interpretability and standardization of colour were raised.

Yes — women with major depression in pregnancy were identifiable in population health data: in a Western Australian record-linkage study, depression during pregnancy was ascertained from two administrative sources, namely dispensing records for antidepressant medicines (WHO ATC 3rd-level pharmacological subgroup 'N06A Antidepressants') and hospital admission records (including the birth admission) carrying a recorded comorbidity relating to depression.

Among 96698 births in Western Australia from 2002 to 2005, at least one antidepressant was dispensed to 4485 (4.6%) pregnant women, and 3010 (3.1%) women had a depression-related comorbidity recorded on their delivery admission or on another admission to hospital during pregnancy.

The two record sets together identified a total of 7495 pregnancies, which data linkage showed represented 6596 individual pregnancies; only 899 pregnancies (13.6% of all cases) appeared in both groups, and 80% of women dispensed an antidepressant had no depression recorded as a hospital comorbidity.
A simple capture-recapture calculation based on the two ascertainment sources suggested a depression prevalence of around 16% in this population of pregnant women.

Because the two administrative sources overlapped only partially, ascertainment of depression in pregnancy from a single dataset would miss cases captured only by the other source, which is a limitation entailed by the study's reliance on routinely collected administrative records rather than a clinical diagnostic assessment.

In a canine model, a solitary kidney was more resistant to warm ischemia than paired kidneys: after 90 minutes of left renal artery occlusion, group 1 (solitary kidney created by right nephrectomy, 10 dogs) showed a smaller fall in clearance and less tubular necrosis than group 2 (10 dogs with both kidneys).

In group 1 (solitary kidney) clearance decreased by 20% at 1 week and basal function was regained starting at week 2, whereas in group 2 (both kidneys) clearance decreased by more than 90% up to week 2, recovery started only at week 3, and by 4 weeks a 23% clearance reduction persisted.

Histopathology showed significant tubular necrosis (60%) at 3 days in group 1 with regeneration starting at 1 week, versus more pronounced tubular necrosis (90%) in group 2 with regeneration starting at 2 weeks.

Expression of the proinflammatory markers CD95 and tumor necrosis factor-α, assessed by real-time polymerase chain reaction, was up-regulated in each group, with higher and more sustained expression in group 2 (both kidneys) than in group 1 (solitary kidney).

The authors state that to their knowledge there were no evidence-based medicine data to date to critically judge the vulnerability of a solitary kidney to warm ischemia compared with paired kidneys, and the comparison reported here derives from a dog model in which right nephrectomy created the solitary kidney, so it does not by itself establish the same differential response in humans.

Bicompartmental knee arthroplasty was not more favourable to knee muscle strength than total knee arthroplasty: in 24 patients (31 knees) prospectively examined preoperatively and at 6 and 12 months after each surgery, isokinetic knee extensor and flexor torque, hamstring/Quadriceps ratio and position sense measured with the Biodex system did not differ significantly between the bicompartmental and TKA groups at any of those time points, and within each group muscle strength and position sense were not different across time points.

Bicompartmental knee arthroplasty was not more favourable to physical performance than total knee arthroplasty: timed up and go test, stair climbing test and 6-min walk test results were not significantly different between the two groups preoperatively or at 6 and 12 months after surgery, although within-group analysis showed both groups improved in the 6-min walk test while only the TKA group showed enhancement in the stair climbing test.

A cross-sectional observational study using convenience sampling of inner-city pediatric emergency department patients in the fall of 2010 characterized the use and delivery of cough and cold medicines in children younger than 6 following the 2007 FDA warnings; 65 patients and their caregivers consented and participated.

In that study, caregivers were presented with 6 commonly used cough medicine preparations and asked to demonstrate if and how they would administer these to their children; 82% (53/65) stated that they would treat with cough or cold medicines.

Yes, concerns still existed in this post-warning cohort: during the demonstration, 72% (38/53) of the caregivers who said they would treat with cough or cold medicines incorrectly dosed the medication they desired to give.

Because the evidence comes from a cross-sectional observational study with convenience sampling of emergency department attendees, it documents reported intended use and dosing errors in that setting but cannot establish trends over time or causal relationships.

The retrieved evidence does not establish sternal skin conductance as a validated surrogate for hot flash measurement: hot flash data from the second prototype of the device showed only a 24% concordance rate between self-reported and device-recorded hot flashes, and a raw concordance figure of this kind does not by itself demonstrate agreement with a reference standard.

The first prototype of the sternal skin conductance device was not able to collect any analyzable skin conductance data because of malfunction issues including poor conductance and battery failure, so it produced no hot flash measurements to compare with women's reports.

The device-based hot flash findings came from three small descriptive pilot studies using two sequential prototypes, worn either in a monitored setting for 24 hours or in an ambulatory setting for 5 weeks; such a descriptive pilot design cannot establish diagnostic validity of the device against a reference standard.

In a separate prospective study of 56 women recently treated for breast cancer who completed a 14-day Hot Flashes and Anxiety Diary, hot flashes were objectively recorded for a continuous 24-hour period using home-based sternal skin conductance; greater anxiety on the diary was significantly associated with a shorter time to reach the hot flash peak as assessed with sternal skin conductance (partial Spearman correlation coefficient rsp = -0.44).

Acceptability was reported by 16 women who wore the sternal skin conductance device for 5 weeks, who reported that wearing the device was acceptable, although 31% stated that it interfered with daily activities.

The device was worn either in a monitored setting for 24 hours or in an ambulatory setting for 5 weeks, and during the study period women recorded hot flashes in a prospective hot flash diary and answered questions about the acceptability of wearing the device.

Adding oblique views did not improve diagnostic performance for spondylolysis in adolescents: in a retrospective review of radiographs from fifty adolescents with L5 spondylolysis without spondylolisthesis and fifty controls confirmed free of spondylolysis by CT, MRI or bone scanning, read by four pediatric spine surgeons, there was no significant difference in sensitivity or specificity between four-view (anteroposterior, lateral, and both obliques) and two-view (anteroposterior and lateral) radiographs; sensitivity was 0.59 for two-view versus 0.53 for four-view studies (p = 0.33) and specificity was 0.96 for two-view versus 0.94 for four-view studies (p = 0.60).

Agreement measures likewise showed no significant difference between the two view sets: inter-rater agreement, intra-rater agreement and agreement with the gold standard (intraclass correlation coefficients) were all in the moderate range with no significant differences, and percent overall agreement was 78% for four-view studies versus 82% for two-view studies.

Against this absence of diagnostic gain, the four-view protocol carried higher radiation exposure and cost: the effective radiation dose was 1.26 mSv for four-view studies versus 0.72 mSv for two-view studies (difference, 0.54 mSv), and the charge for four-view studies was $145 more than for two-view studies.

In this nationally representative sample of 1,418 women who were sterile from a tubal sterilization, 78% had a history of at least one unintended pregnancy and 28% expressed a desire to have their sterilization reversed.
Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the relationship between a history of unintended pregnancy and desire for sterilization reversal while controlling for potential confounders.

In unadjusted analysis, having a prior unintended pregnancy was associated with higher odds of expressing desire for sterilization reversal (odds ratio [OR]: 1.80; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.15-2.79), whereas in adjusted analysis controlling for sociodemographic factors, unintended pregnancy was no longer significantly associated with desire for reversal (OR: 1.46; 95% CI: 0.91-2.34).
This study used national, cross-sectional data collected by the 2006-2010 National Survey of Family Growth.

Because the analysis used national, cross-sectional survey data collected by the 2006-2010 National Survey of Family Growth, the reported association between a history of unintended pregnancy and desire for sterilization reversal cannot establish that unintended pregnancy causes a change in women's desire for reversal.

Yes, most patients received the management recommended by the multidisciplinary breast cancer team: in a single-centre audit of all referrals to a breast multidisciplinary team (MDT) with breast cancer diagnosed between 1 July 2009 and 30 June 2011, MDT decisions were compared with subsequent patient management and classified as concordant or discordant, and 91.5% (2956 of 3230) of decisions were concordant, 4.5% (146 of 3230) were discordant, and 4% (128 of 3230) had no MDT decision.
Over the study period the audit covered 3230 MDT decisions relating to 705 patients.
Among the 146 discordant decisions, 26 (17.8%) were considered 'unjustifiable' because no additional information was available after the MDT to account for the change in management.

The remaining 120 discordant MDT decisions were considered 'justifiable', as management was altered because of patient choice (n=61), additional information available after the MDT (n=54), or MDT error (n=5).

Calibration is not supported as the cause of variation in LC-MS/MS testosterone measurement: in a study in which 15 laboratories analysed seven serum samples using their own in-house calibrators, the variation in results did not improve when the results were corrected with a common calibrator.

The same study reported no consensus among participating laboratories on the supplier of testosterone or the matrix used for preparing calibrators, with all calibrators prepared in-house, and found that a wide variety of mass spectrometers, internal standards, chromatography conditions and sample extractions were used.

Because the analysis relied on results returned by laboratories using their own calibrators, the finding that a common calibrator correction did not reduce variation does not by itself establish which of the other differing methodological factors caused the between-assay variation.

In a two-year audit of the implementation of epidural analgesia for labor, epidural analgesia rose from 15.5% of all labors in the first trimester of the study to 51% in the last trimester (p<0.005), showing that implementation was not universal across all labors during the audit period.

The audit cycle measured epidural analgesia performance against 4 standards: (1) implementation of epidural analgesia for labor to all patients, (2) acceptance and good satisfaction level reported by patients and caregivers, (3) effectiveness of labor analgesia, and (4) no maternal or fetal side effects.
The study reports that social and cultural factors combined with little information may prevent the diffusion of epidural analgesia for pain relief during childbirth.
A hierarchical clustering analysis based on VAS time course identified two groups: 226 patients (cluster 1) and 1002 patients (cluster 2).

Satisfaction levels reported by patients and care givers were good, and for the effectiveness standard the VAS in the 226 patients of cluster 1 decreased from 8.5±1.4 before to 4.1±1.3 after epidural analgesia, whereas in the 1002 patients of cluster 2 it decreased from 8.12±1.7 before (NS vs cluster 1) to 0.76±0.79 after (p<0.001 vs before and vs cluster 2 after).
No other differences between the two clusters were observed.

Because the evidence comes from an audit cycle measuring performance against four standards rather than a comparative trial, the reported VAS reductions describe analgesia performance within the two identified clusters and do not establish that the effectiveness standard was reached by every woman.

No: in a randomized clinical trial, 45 patients requiring upper first premolar extractions were randomly allocated into one of three groups: (1) conventional pre-adjusted edgewise brackets and elastomeric ligatures; (2) conventional pre-adjusted edgewise brackets and Super Slick(®) low friction elastomeric ligatures; (3) Damon 3MX(®) passive self-ligating brackets.
The primary outcome measure was the mean amount of space closure in a 3-month period.
The amount of space closure was very similar between the three groups (1 mm per 28 days); however, there was a wide variation in the rate of space closure between individuals.
The differences in the amount of space closure over three months between the three groups was very small and non-significant (P = 0·718).
