Yes — in the matched-pair analysis of open total mesorectal excision (TME) reported in PMID:23810330, intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) was associated with better urogenital and anorectal functional outcome: newly developed urinary dysfunction after surgery occurred in 1 of 15 IONM patients versus 6 of 15 controls (p = 0.031), and impaired anorectal function at follow up was present in 1 of 15 patients undergoing TME with IONM versus 6 of 15 without IONM (p = 0.031).
In the same open-TME comparison, postoperative residual urine volume was significantly higher in the control group (no IONM) than in the IONM group.
The IONM group showed a trend towards a lower rate of sexual dysfunction after surgery, which was not reported as a statistically significant difference.

The findings come from a consecutive series of 150 patients with primary rectal cancer, from which 15 match pairs with open TME and combined urogenital and anorectal functional assessment at follow up were established, identical with respect to gender, tumour site, tumour stage, neoadjuvant radiotherapy and type of surgery; function was evaluated prospectively using self-administered standardized questionnaires, residual urine volume measurement and long-term catheterization rate.

Because these results derive from a matched-pair comparison of a consecutive series rather than a randomised comparison, the design cannot by itself establish that IONM causes the observed functional differences, and the reported sexual-dysfunction finding is a trend rather than a significant difference.

The cited evidence does not establish that oxybutynin hydrochloride causes arrhythmia specifically in children with bladder dysfunction; the available report describes a subset of children admitted to Pediatric Surgery and Pediatric Nephrology Clinics between January 2011 and July 2012 and states that the QT interval changed significantly depending on oxybutynin use and that the QT changes increased cardiac arrhythmia in children.

In that subset, the reported population was defined by clinic admission (Pediatric Surgery and Pediatric Nephrology) rather than by a diagnosis of bladder dysfunction, so the arrhythmia finding is not attributed to children with bladder dysfunction.
Because the report describes a subset of a complete data set rather than a controlled comparison, it cannot by itself establish that oxybutynin use causes arrhythmia.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Arrhythmia specifically in children with bladder dysfunction.

Yes — in the SEARCH database study, all four postoperative nomograms predicted PCSM more accurately than they predicted BCR, with higher c-index values, and each nomogram could predict aggressive BCR and PCSM in a statistically significant manner. the authors performed Cox analyses to examine the ability of 4 postoperative nomograms, the Duke Prostate Center (DPC) nomogram, the Kattan postoperative nomogram, the Johns Hopkins Hospital (JHH) nomogram, and the joint Center for Prostate Disease Research(CPDR)/Cancer of the Prostate Strategic Urologic Research Endeavor (CaPSURE) nomogram to predict BCR and PCSM among 1778 men in the Shared Equal Access Regional Cancer Hospital (SEARCH) database who underwent RP between 1990 and 2009. the authors calculated the c-index for each nomogram to determine its predictive accuracy for estimating actual outcomes. the authors also compared their ability to predict BCR and aggressive BCR in a subset of men.
A previous study showed that several nomograms could predict aggressive BCR (prostate-specific antigen doubling time [PSADT] <9 months) more accurately than BCR.
However, it remains unknown if they can predict more definitive endpoints, such as PCSM.

The stated objective was to examine the ability of various postoperative nomograms to predict prostate cancer-specific mortality (PCSM) and to validate that they could predict aggressive biochemical recurrence (BCR). the authors found that each nomogram could predict aggressive BCR and PCSM in a statistically significant manner and that they all predicted PCSM more accurately than they predicted BCR (ie, with higher c-index values).

Yes — in a retrospective matched cohort, intraoperative precursor events were associated with postoperative major adverse events: the incidence of the individual precursor events of bleeding and of difficulty weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass was significantly higher in the postoperative MACE group than in its matched non-MACE comparison group.

The study was a retrospective cohort design performed at the Queen Elizabeth Health Science Centre, in which low- to medium-risk patients who had experienced postoperative MACE were matched 1:1 with patients who had not experienced postoperative MACE, and a total of 311 MACE patients (98.4%) were matched.

The operative notes, for both the MACE and non-MACE groups, were scored by 5 surgeons to determine the frequency of 4 precursor events — bleeding, difficulty weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass, repair or regrafting, and incomplete revascularization or repair — and a univariate comparison of ≥1 precursor events in the matched groups was performed.
The primary outcome occurred more frequently in the MACE group than in the non-MACE group (33% vs 24%; P =.015).

The study's purpose was to determine whether precursor events are associated with a composite endpoint of major adverse cardiac events (MACE) comprising death, acute renal failure, stroke, and infection in a low- to medium-risk coronary artery bypass grafting, valve, and valve plus coronary artery bypass grafting population.

Because the reported design is a retrospective cohort with matched groups, the observed association between intraoperative precursor events and postoperative MACE cannot by itself establish that preventing or modifying precursor events would improve postoperative outcomes.

The cited evidence indicates that maintaining viral load suppression was feasible in a resource-limited setting: the study was conducted to assess these questions in a resource-limited setting, and consisted of a retrospective observational study of HIV-infected patients diagnosed in the pre-HAART era on follow-up at a private center in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in which 82 of 619 patients on follow-up (13.2%) had been diagnosed in the pre-HAART era.

In the Buenos Aires retrospective observational study, 79 of the 82 pre-HAART-era patients (96.3%) were on HAART with a median duration of 14 years of therapy (IQR 12-15), 69 (87.3%) had undetectable viral load, 37 (46.8%) had never presented virologic failure and 19 (24.1%) had experienced only one failure, while 13 (16.5%) were receiving third-line ART regimens and had on average 2.7-fold more virologic failures than patients on first- or second-line regimens (p = 0.007).

In a separate study of 93 patients with a mean age of 45.6 years, of whom 25.8% were AIDS patients, 82.8% had an HIV viral load under 50 copies/ml and the mean duration of treatment was 6.23 years; in univariate and multivariate analysis, knowledge of dosage was correlated with a controlled viral load (P = 0.04), an association that does not by itself establish that improving dosage knowledge causes viral control.

Orthostatic myoclonus (OM) has been suggested as a cause of gait impairment and unsteadiness in neurodegenerative diseases, and in a retrospective analysis of clinical data and electromyogram surface recordings from 93 subjects with unexplained unsteadiness/gait impairment, all 16 patients diagnosed with OM complained of unsteadiness during orthostatism and/or during gait.

In that series, leg jerking was observed by visual inspection during orthostatism in only four subjects, two of whom also presented falls, and 11 of the 16 OM patients (68.7%) had an associated neurodegenerative disease such as multiple system atrophy (n = 3), Parkinson's disease (n = 2), Alzheimer's disease (n = 2), mild cognitive impairment (n = 2) and normal pressure hydrocephalus (n = 2).
Among the 93 subjects studied, OM was the most frequent disorder (n = 16; 17.2%), followed by orthostatic tremor (13.9%) and low frequency tremors during orthostatism (12.9%).

Because this frequency finding comes from a retrospective analysis of a selected series of subjects with unexplained unsteadiness or gait impairment rather than a population-based sample, the cited data establish OM's relative frequency in that referral cohort but do not by themselves quantify how often OM is missed in the broader patient population.

Urinary NAG, urinary alpha-1-microglobulin, albuminuria, and eGFR (CKD-EPI equation) were measured in a study analyzing the significance of urinary biomarkers in the assessment of tubulointerstitial lesions of the SK.

A cross-sectional study of 37 patients with SK included 18 patients with acquired SK (mean age 56.44 ± 12.20 years, interval from nephrectomy 10.94 ± 9.37 years) and 19 patients with congenital SK (mean age 41.52 ± 10.54 years).
In acquired SK, NAG increased in 60.66%, urinary alpha 1-microglobulin in 16.66%, and albuminuria in 55.55% of patients.
Inverse correlation with eGFR presented NAG (R(2 )= 0.537, p = 0.022), urinary alpha 1-microglobulin (R(2 )= 0.702, p = 0.001), and albuminuria (R(2 )= 0.655, p = 0.003).
In congenital SK, NAG increased in 52.63%, urinary alpha 1-microglobulin in 5.26%, and albuminuria in 47.36% of patients.
In this group, urinary biomarkers correlated inversely with eGFR: NAG (R(2 )= 0.743, p < 0.001), urinary alpha 1-microglobulin (R(2 )= 0.701, p = 0.001), and albuminuria (R(2 )= 0.821, p < 0.001).
Significant correlations were found between the urinary biomarkers in both groups.

Because the study was cross-sectional, the reported inverse associations between urinary biomarkers and eGFR cannot establish that changes in these urinary biomarkers precede or cause progression of tubulointerstitial lesions in the solitary kidney.

Yes — in a retrospective series of 425 consecutive patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma treated between January 2006 and December 2008, preoperative platelet count was an independent prognostic factor on multivariate analysis (P = 0.013), together with T grade (P = 0.017) and N staging (P < 0.001).

A receiver operating characteristic curve for survival prediction was plotted to verify the optimum cutoff point for preoperative platelet count, which was 205 × 10(9)/L; univariate and multivariate analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic parameters.
Patients with a preoperative platelet count of 205 × 10(9)/L or less had a significantly better 5-year survival than those with a count above 205 (60.7% vs.
Among node-negative patients, 5-year survival was similar for those with platelet count 205 × 10(9)/L or less and those above 205 (68.6% vs.
Among patients with involved nodes, 5-year survival was better for those with platelet count 205 × 10(9)/L or less than for those above 205 (32.0% vs.

Because the evidence comes from a retrospective analysis of consecutive patients rather than a prospective design, it establishes an association between preoperative platelet count and survival in ESCC but does not establish that modifying platelet count would change clinical outcomes.

In the Danish 1905 Cohort Survey (nationwide, longitudinal, all individuals born in Denmark in 1905; 2,262 persons aged 92 or 93 at the 1998 baseline), an optimistic outlook did predict better survival among the oldest-old: univariable analyses showed optimistic women and men at lower risk of death than their neutral counterparts, although the association weakened once confounders were accounted for.
During the 12-year follow-up (1998-2010) there were 2,239 deaths (99%) in the 1905 Cohort Survey.

In univariable analyses, optimistic women had a lower risk of death than neutral women (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.73-0.93) and optimistic men had a lower risk of death than neutral men (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.66-0.99).

After adjustment for confounding factors such as baseline physical and cognitive functioning and disease, the optimism-survival association weakened in both sexes but the general pattern persisted: optimistic women remained at lower risk of death than neutral women (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.74-0.97), while the decreased risk among optimistic men relative to neutral men was non-significant (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.73-1.13).

Covering the resection margin after distal pancreatectomy was not shown to be advantageous: in a retrospective analysis of 74 distal pancreatectomies, complication-free rates (23/42, 55% with coverage vs.
16/32, 50% without) and postoperative bleeding rates (12% with coverage vs.
13% without) were similar, pancreatic fistulas were not significantly different (7/32, 22% without coverage vs.
4/42 with coverage), and hospital stay was shorter in patients without coverage (13 days, range 5-60) than with coverage (17 days, range 8-60).

The comparison rests on a retrospective analysis of data from 74 patients who underwent distal pancreatectomy between 2001 and 2011 at the community hospital in Neuss, in which patients with coverage of the resection margins were compared with those without coverage for demographics, indications, postoperative complications, surgical or interventional revisions and length of hospital stay.

Postoperative complications were absent in 23/42 (55%) patients with coverage versus 16/32 (50%) patients without coverage of the resection margins, and across the whole cohort 39 of 74 (53%) patients had no postoperative complications.
Pancreatic fistulas occurred in 7/32 (22%) patients without coverage of the resection margins versus 4/42 patients with coverage, a difference that did not reach statistical significance.
Postoperative bleeding occurred with equal frequency in both groups: 12% with coverage versus 13% without coverage of the resection margins.
The hospital stay was 13 days (range 5-60) for patients without coverage versus 17 days (range 8-60) for patients with coverage of the resection margins.

Because the analysis was a single-centre retrospective comparison, it can describe associations between margin coverage and these postoperative outcomes but cannot establish that covering the resection margin causes any change in complications, fistula, bleeding or hospital stay.

In a single-institution retrospective analysis of 2,301 patients who underwent laparoscopic adjustable gastric banding with hiatal hernia repair between July 1, 2007 and December 31, 2011, the number and location of sutures were the independent variables studied, and the majority of patients received one suture (range 1-6; 55%), with anterior suture placement (vs posterior vs both) being most common (61%).

In that series, patients with fewer sutures had shorter operating room time (1 suture 45 min vs 4+ sutures 56 min, p<0.0001), and OR time was also shorter with anterior suture placement (anterior 41 min vs posterior 56 min vs both 59 min, p<0.0001); length of stay, 30-day readmission, band-related reoperation and postoperative BMI/%EWL were not statistically significant across suture-number groups, whereas patients with a posterior suture had a longer length of stay (84% 1 day vs anterior 74% 1 day vs both 74% 1 day, p<0.0001), with no difference in 30-day readmission, band-related reoperation, and postoperative BMI/%EWL across suture-location groups.

Because this was a retrospective analysis, the reported associations between suture number or location and operative time, length of stay or reoperation cannot establish that changing suture technique causes these outcomes to change.

In PMID:23759406, behavioral health care for youth with poorly controlled type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and their caregivers was compared when delivered in-clinic versus delivered by Internet-based videoconferencing (Skype), with the therapeutic alliance as the outcome of interest.

Seventy-one adolescents with poorly controlled T1DM (hemoglobin A1c ≥9%) and one of their caregivers each received up to 10 sessions of a family-based behavioral health intervention previously shown to improve adherence to diabetes regimens and family functioning, and 32 of them were randomized to the Skype condition.
No significant differences in working alliance inventory (WAI) scores were found between those receiving behavioral health care via Skype and those receiving it in-clinic.

In PMID:24139705, each patient received a smartphone with an insulin dose advisor (IDA), with (G3 group) or without (G2 group) the telemonitoring/teleconsultation function, and the respective impact of the IDA function and teleconsultations on the final HbA1c levels was analyzed.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: telemedicine technology alone improves glycaemic control (HbA1c) in type 1 diabetes.

Serum CA125 and CA72-4 were measured in 72 patients with ovarian endometriomas and 55 patients with ovarian cancer, and a marked difference in CA72-4 values was observed between the women with ovarian cancer (71.0%) and the patients with endometriosis (13.8%) (P<0.0001), indicating that CA72-4 is useful in the differential diagnosis between ovarian endometrioma and epithelial ovarian cancer.

In the same study, CA125 concentrations were high both in patients with ovarian endometriosis and in those with ovarian cancer, so this marker was not useful for discriminating ovarian endometrioma from ovarian malignancy.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: the 7th edition TNM node staging predicts biological/clinical behavior in early gastric cancer.

In an ex vivo study using 52 bone blocks extracted from fresh bovine pelvic bone, intergroup comparison showed lower levels of primary stability when the trabecular bone mineral density (BMD) was lower and when cortical bone was absent (P≤.05); primary stability was evaluated with miniscrews 1.4 mm in diameter and 6 mm long using insertion torque (IT), mini-implant mobility (PTV), and pull-out strength (PS).
In the same bovine bone-block study, Pearson correlation testing showed correlation between trabecular number, trabecular thickness, BV/TV, trabecular BMD, and total BMD and IT, PTV, and PS.
Specimens were micro-computed tomography imaged to evaluate trabecular thickness, trabecular number, trabecular separation, bone volume density (BV/TV), BMD, and cortical thickness.

Because these findings come from extracted bovine bone blocks tested ex vivo rather than from patients, they establish an association between trabecular properties and primary stability measurements in that model and cannot by themselves establish clinical miniscrew success or failure in human jaws.

Digoxin is a commonly used medication for heart failure and cardiac arrhythmias that has been suggested as a novel chemotherapeutic agent, and preclinical studies of prostate cancer (PCa) have shown anti-tumor activity with digoxin; this study explored the relationship between digoxin use and PCa risk.

Data came from a population-based case-control study of incident cases aged 35-74 years at PCa diagnosis in 2002-2005 in King County, Washington; controls were identified by random digit dialing and frequency matched by age, digoxin use was determined from in-person questionnaires regarding medical and prescription history, and the relationship of digoxin use with PCa risk was evaluated with logistic regression.
One thousand one cases of PCa and 942 controls were analyzed; the prevalence of digoxin use in controls was 2.7%, and use was positively correlated with age.

In multivariate analysis adjusting for age, race, PSA screening, and family history of PCa, digoxin use was associated with a reduction in the odds ratio of PCa (OR 0.58, 95% CI: 0.30-1.10); the confidence interval includes 1.0, so this estimate was not statistically significant.
Among those with ≥3 PSA tests over the preceding 5 years (546 cases, 380 controls), digoxin use was associated with a stronger reduction of PCa risk (OR 0.44, 95% CI: 0.20-0.98).

Because this is an observational case-control study in which digoxin use was ascertained by in-person questionnaire after PCa diagnosis, the reported association does not establish the effect of intervening on digoxin exposure on prostate cancer risk.

The retrieved evidence does not establish that routinely collected ambulance data about assaults reduces community violence: the only cited study is a 12-month (2012) descriptive analysis of spatiotemporal clusters of police and ambulance calls for service, which notes that little is known about interagency 'data-crossover' despite some developments through the Cardiff Model, and it reports no violence-reduction outcome.

That study analysed 3,775 violent crime incidents and 775 assault incidents using spatiotemporal clustering with a k-means++ algorithm and Spearman's rho, and found that calls for service to the police and the ambulance service are equally highly concentrated in a small number of geographical areas, primarily within intra-agency hotspots (33% of police calls and 53% of ambulance calls) and also across the other agency's hotspots (25% and 15%, respectively).
The police and ambulance datasets were statistically correlated with one another at the 0.57 and 0.34 levels, with 50% overlap when adjusted for the number of hotspots.

At least one in every two police hotspots did not have an ambulance hotspot overlapping with it, which the authors interpret as suggesting that half of assault spatiotemporal concentrations are unknown to the police.
The data further suggest that more severely injured patients, as estimated by transfer to hospital, tend to be injured in the places with the highest number of police-recorded crimes.

Because the cited work is a descriptive, cross-sectional-style analysis of hotspot location and overlap in one 12-month period, it can show where police and ambulance data converge or diverge but cannot establish that using routinely collected ambulance assault data brings about a reduction in community violence.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: actual reduction in community violence following use of routinely collected ambulance data about assaults.

Yes — most of the athletes who had ventricular premature beats and/or ventricular couplets and/or non-sustained ventricular tachycardia during their initial exercise test had far fewer ventricular arrhythmias in the follow-up exercise test (P = 0.001).

From a database of 56,462 athletes, 192 athletes (aged <35 years) who had ventricular arrhythmias during an exercise test were identified: 90 athletes had ≥3 ventricular premature beats (group A) and 102 athletes had ventricular couplets or non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (group B); a control group of 92 athletes without ventricular arrhythmias was randomly selected from the database (group C).

Of the 192 athletes, 39 returned for a repeat exercise test after a mean follow-up period of 70 ± 25 months and constituted the study population; 12 athletes from group A, 21 from group B and 6 from group C returned for a repeat exercise test.

A follow-up survey of 199 patients identified from the cohort of all patients recognized by the Danish National Board of Industrial Injuries in 2010 as having occupational dermatitis, who had relevant rubber allergy (contact allergy to rubber chemicals or contact urticaria from latex) or epoxy allergy, assessed prognosis 2 years after recognition of occupational allergic contact dermatitis using a questionnaire covering current severity of eczema, employment, exposure and quality of life; the response rate was 75%.
In that 2-year follow-up, clearance of eczema was reported by 11% of patients and 67% reported improvement.

Total clearance of eczema was reported by 22% of patients allergic to a nonubiquitous allergen (epoxy) compared with 10% of those allergic to ubiquitous allergens (rubber chemicals and latex) and 0% of those with contact urticaria, a difference with a reported P value of 0·116, i.e. not statistically significant.

Eighty male Wistar rats were divided into eight groups (n = 10); in the first four groups, non-ischemic colonic anastomosis was performed, whereas in the remaining four groups, ischemic colonic anastomosis was performed.
In groups 5, 6, 7, and 8, colonic ischemia was established by ligating 2 cm of the mesocolon on either side of the anastomosis.

The control groups (1 and 5) received no treatment; hyperbaric oxygen therapy was initiated immediately after surgery and continued for 4 days in groups 3 and 4; groups 2 and 6 received recombinant human growth hormone, whereas groups 4 and 8 received GH and hyperbaric oxygen treatment.

Relaparotomy was performed on postoperative day 4, and a perianastomotic colon segment 2 cm in length was excised for the detection of biochemical and mechanical parameters of anastomotic healing and histopathological evaluation.

Combined treatment with hyperbaric oxygen and GH increased the mean bursting pressure values in all of the groups, and a statistically significant increase was noted in the ischemic groups compared to the controls (p<0.05).
This improvement was more evident in the ischemic and normal groups treated with combined therapy.
A histopathological evaluation of anastomotic neovascularization and collagen deposition showed significant differences among the groups.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: direct comparison with growth hormone or hyperbaric oxygen alone; left colon location.

In a cross-sectional observational study of 207 patients without any atherosclerotic disease history, correlation analysis (Pearson and Spearman tests) between epicardial fat tissue thickness measured by echocardiography and serum paraoxonase 1 (PON 1) level found no linear correlation (correlation coefficient -0.127, p=0.069).
When the same patients were grouped by epicardial fat tissue thickness, serum PON 1 level was significantly lower in the ≥7 mm group (168.9 U/L) than in the <7 mm group (253.9 U/L) (p<0.001).

In a cadaveric model, four examiners measured Schanz pin protrusion beyond the distal cortices using ultrasonography first and then by direct measurement after gross dissection; 16 Schanz pins had been equally placed in bilateral femora and tibiae.

Schanz pin protrusion measurements were underestimated by ultrasonography (p<0.01) by an average of 10 percent over the range of 5 to 18 mm, and showed a proportional bias that increased the under-reporting as the magnitude of pin protrusion increased.
Ultrasound data demonstrated good linear correlation and closely represented actual protrusion values in the 5 to 12 mm range.
Interobserver repeatability analysis demonstrated that all examiners were not statistically different in their measurements despite minimal familiarity with the ultrasound methodology (p>0.8).
Cadaveric preparation and observations were done by an orthopaedic traumatologist and resident, and two general surgery traumatologists.

The source evaluated ultrasonography in a cadaveric model and did not specify use of a portable ultrasound device; therefore, the accuracy of portable ultrasonography itself for evaluating Schanz pin placement is not established, and the reported cadaveric results apply to ultrasonography generally.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Portable-device accuracy of ultrasonography for Schanz pin placement.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Accuracy of portable ultrasonography for Schanz pin placement in austere or field environments.

In the prospective randomized study reported in PMID:24476003, nasogastric decompression did not prevent staple line leaks after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: one staple line leak (1.4%) occurred on the 6th postoperative day among the 70 group A patients whose operations were completed with placement of a nasogastric tube, whereas no leak was observed in the 75 group B patients in whom no nasogastric tube was placed.

The study aimed to evaluate whether gastric decompression can play a role in avoiding the occurrence of staple line leaks after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy, and it prospectively and randomly included 145 patients between January 2008 and November 2012; the report notes that no author had previously investigated the role of gastric decompression in preventing this complication.

In the Los Angeles Police Department Reporting Districts study (January 2006-December 2008), reported crime rates were negatively associated with over-the-counter (OTC) syringe sales after adjustment for potential confounders using generalized estimating equations (adjusted rate ratio: 0.89; 95% confidence interval: 0.81, 0.99), indicating no positive association between OTC syringe sales and reported crime.

The study used a geographic information system together with spatial and longitudinal analyses to determine whether implementation of pharmacy-based OTC syringe sales was associated with reported crime, assessing reported crime both pre- and post-OTC syringe sales initiation and longitudinal associations between crime and OTC syringe-selling pharmacies.
Overall reported crime counts and reported crime rates decreased between 2006 and 2008 in all 1010 Reporting Districts.

Because the evidence comes from an observational geographic and longitudinal association analysis of reported crime in Police Department Reporting Districts, it can describe associations between OTC syringe sales and reported crime but cannot establish that OTC syringe sales cause changes in crime.

In 79 adjacent proximal surfaces of permanent teeth without restorations, radiographic assessment recording lesions with or without cavitation by two observers in bitewings and CBCT sections (Kodak 9000 3D, 5 x 3.7 cm field of view, 0.07 mm voxel size) showed that CBCT reporting of proximal cavitation achieved significantly higher sensitivity than bitewings (average difference 33%, p<0.001), with specificity not significantly different between the two modalities (p=0.19) and overall accuracy also significantly higher for CBCT (p<0.001); differences between modalities were estimated by analyzing the binary data in a generalized linear model.

The reference standard for cavitation status in that assessment was clinical validation: orthodontic separators were placed interdentally between two lesion-suspected surfaces, removed after 3 days, and the surfaces then recorded as cavitated (yes/no).

The study reports significantly higher sensitivity (average difference 33%, p<0.001) and significantly higher overall accuracy (p<0.001) for CBCT than bitewings, with specificity not significantly different (p=0.19).

Because this was a diagnostic accuracy study in patients suspected of having carious lesions after visual clinical and bitewing examination, its results on relative sensitivity, specificity and accuracy do not by themselves establish a practice recommendation or a demonstrated clinical benefit of reporting proximal cavitation on CBCT.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: formal practice recommendation or demonstrated clinical benefit.

Yes — determination of specific IgE against components with ISAC 112 was reported as a reproducible technique, with very good intra- and inter-assay agreement for 94 allergens and good agreement for one.

Reliability of the ISAC 112 technique was studied intra- and inter-assay and inter-batch- and inter-laboratory-assay in 20 samples consisting of 19 sera from polysensitized allergic patients plus the manufacturer's calibrator (CTR02); CTR02 and three patients' sera were measured ten times in the same and in different assays, and all samples were tested in two laboratories and with two batches of ISAC kit.

Precision was assessed by the coefficient of variation (CV) of the 15 allergens generating the calibration curve, while repeatability and reproducibility were assessed by the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) calculated for each allergen.
In the inter-batch analysis, very good agreement was obtained for 82 allergens, good for 14, moderate for 5, poor for 1 and bad for 1 allergen.
In the inter-laboratory analysis, very good agreement was obtained for 73 allergens, good for 22, moderate for 6 and poor for 2 allergens.
The mean CV obtained in the CTR02 determinations was 9.4%, while the variability of the patients' sera was 22.9%.

Yes — in the cited single study of 23 consecutive suspected carotid free-floating thrombus (FFT) cases seen on CTA, quantitative shape analysis differentiated true-positive FFT from atherosclerotic plaque, with the logistic regression model built from all five shape features achieving a sensitivity of 87.5%, a specificity of 71.4% and an area under the ROC curve of 0.85 ± 0.09.

The cohort comprised 23 consecutive cases of suspected carotid FFT on CTA (13 men, 65 ± 10 years; 10 women, 65.5 ± 8.8 years), in which FFT+ was defined as a filling defect resolving with anticoagulant therapy and FFT- as one remaining unchanged, with follow-up imaging confirming sixteen FFT+ and seven FFT- cases.

Lesion volumes were extracted from the CTA images and quantitative shape descriptors computed; the five most discriminative features were used to construct ROC curves and to generate three machine-learning classifiers, with average classification accuracy determined by cross-validation and average accuracy for each classifier ranging from 65.2% to 76.4%.

Five shape descriptors delineated FFT+ from FFT- cases, and combining all five shape features in the logistic regression model yielded the reported sensitivity of 87.5% and specificity of 71.4% with AUC = 0.85 ± 0.09.

Strategy training did not appreciably reduce the age-related working memory deficit: both young and older adults were able to apply the trained strategies on the working memory task and improved their working memory performance after training, but the age-related working memory deficit was not greatly affected and the training gains did not transfer to the other cognitive tasks.

In that experiment, the training group (older adults n = 39; young adults n = 41) was taught verbal encoding strategies and their differential effectiveness and was trained to use interactive imagery and sentence generation on a list-learning task, while the control group (older n = 37; young n = 38) completed an equally engaging filler task.

All participants completed a pre- and post-training reading span task that included self-reported strategy use plus two transfer tasks differing in the affordance to use the trained strategies (a paired-associate recall task and the self-ordered pointing task); participants attempted to adapt the trained strategies for the paired-associate recall task, but the increased strategy use did not benefit their performance.

Yes — in the cited single series of postoperative cerebrospinal fluid fistulas after spine surgery, the ten patients treated with an external lumbar CSF drain for ten days were cured in a mean of 10 days versus a mean of 30 days for the six patients treated conservatively, and all patients healed their wound properly with no adverse events recorded.
Postoperative CSF fistulas were described in 16 of 198 patients (8%) who underwent spine surgery between 2009 and 2010, and the mean follow-up period was ten months.
Six of these patients were treated conservatively by positioning prone for three weeks, while ten were treated by placing an external CSF lumbar drainage for ten days.

The therapeutic strategy was chosen according to the patients' clinical condition, including the feasibility of continuous prone positioning and the morbidity risk of prolonged bed rest, so the reported healing times come from a non-randomized comparison in which the faster healing in the drained group cannot be attributed to lumbar drainage alone.

Yes — in a retrospective analysis of the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database, elderly patients with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) received less treatment: a significant increase was observed in the number of patients who did not receive treatment (surgery, radiation, or combined therapy) after age 55.

The analysis was based on 14,909 patients with OPSCC diagnosed from 2004 to 2009, categorized into age groups 45 to 54, 55 to 64, 65 to 74, 75 to 84, and 85 years and older, and then by treatment status.

Kaplan-Meier analysis of disease-specific survival in late-stage (III and IV) OPSCC showed that the age groups 65 to 74 and 75 to 84 had substantial benefits in DSS with surgery, radiation, or combined therapy.
Multivariable analysis did not demonstrate any statistically significant difference in the hazard ratios for combined treatment among the age groups 45 to 54, 55 to 64, 65 to 74, and 75 to 84.

Because this was a retrospective analysis of a population database, the observed lower receipt of treatment at older ages is an association in the data and cannot by itself establish that age-based withholding of therapy causes the survival differences observed.

HFNC were not noisier than bubble CPAP in preterm infants: there was no evidence of a difference in average noise levels measured at the external auditory meatus, with a mean difference (95% CI) of -1.6 (-4.0 to 0.9) dBA for HFNC compared to BCPAP.
At low frequency (500 Hz), HFNC was mean (95% CI) 3.0 (0.3 to 5.7) dBA quieter than BCPAP.

These findings come from an observational study of preterm infants receiving HFNC or BCPAP in which noise within the external auditory meatus was measured with a microphone probe tube connected to a calibrated digital dosimeter across a range of frequencies and reported as dBA; 21 HFNC and 13 BCPAP noise measurements were performed in 21 infants, with HFNC gas flows of 2-5 L/min and BCPAP gas flows of 6-10 L/min at set pressures of 5-7 cm of water.
Yes: the Disposable Antibacterial Coating (DAC) hydrogel combined with various antibacterial compounds showed both a bactericidal and an antibiofilm effect in vitro.

In that in vitro work, antibacterial activity was determined by broth microdilution and antibiofilm activity by a crystal violet assay, and complete release of all tested antibacterial compounds from the hydrogel was observed in less than 96 hours.
The ability of the DAC hydrogel to deliver antibacterial agents was tested using spectrophotometry and a microbiologic assay.
Coating resistance to press-fit insertion was tested in rabbit tibias and human femurs, and approximately 80% of the hydrogel coating was retrieved on the implant after press-fit insertion.

The press-fit insertion experiments in rabbit tibias and human femurs assessed coating retention on the implant rather than in vitro antibacterial efficacy, so they do not provide additional in vitro evidence on bacterial colonization or biofilm formation.
The primary outcomes examined were postoperative complications and in-hospital mortality.

Univariate analyses and subsequently multivariate analyses, controlling for patient and hospital characteristics, were performed to identify whether the time of surgery was an independent predictor of outcome after major cancer surgery.
On univariate analysis, the overall postoperative complication rate, as well as genitourinary and hematologic complications specifically, was higher in July than the rest of the year.

However, on multivariate analysis, only hematologic complications were significantly higher in July, with no difference in overall postoperative complication rate or in-hospital mortality for all 8 surgeries considered separately or together.
The analysis used the Nationwide Inpatient Sample to abstract data on patients undergoing 1 of 8 major cancer surgeries at academic medical centres between Jan.
1, 1999, and Dec.

Because the findings come from an observational administrative-database analysis rather than a randomized or interventional design, the reported July associations for hematologic complications cannot establish that the timing of surgery causes the outcome.

Yes — in a single-centre study of 538 patients with ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI), a higher SYNTAX score (SxS) was associated with worse in-hospital outcomes, with the high SxS group (>22) showing more no-reflow, lower ejection fraction, and higher re-infarction and mortality rates than the low SxS group (<22).

The study was motivated by the fact that the prognostic value of the SYNTAX score in acute coronary syndrome was still unknown, and its stated aim was to evaluate whether SxS could predict in-hospital outcomes for patients admitted with STEMI who undergo pPCI.
The analysis included 538 patients with STEMI who underwent pPCI between January 2010 and December 2012, divided into a low SxS group (<22) and a high SxS group (>22).

Compared with the low SxS group, the high SxS group had more no-reflow (41% vs 25.1%, p<0.001), lower ejection fraction (38.2 ± 7.5% vs 44.6 ± 8.8%, p<0.001), and greater rates of re-infarction (9.5% vs 7.3%, p = 0.037) and mortality (0.9% vs 0.2%, p = 0.021) during hospitalisation.
On multivariate logistic regression analysis including clinical variables, SxS was an independent predictor of no-reflow (OR 1.081, 95% CI 1.032–1.133, p = 0.001).

As these in-hospital findings come from an observational cohort comparison, they establish an association between higher SYNTAX score and worse in-hospital outcomes rather than demonstrating that modifying the SYNTAX score itself improves outcomes.

Bottom line: in an interrupted time-series analysis of real Oklahoma Medicaid claims (January 2006 through December 2009) for 9289 continuously eligible members with epilepsy and/or psychiatric disorder and at least one AED prescription claim, AED prescription claims did not change significantly after the FDA suicidality warning, with no significant change in trend detected during or after the warning relative to the prewarning period.

Trends, expressed as monthly changes in the log odds of AED prescription claims, were compared across three periods: before the FDA warning (January 2006 to January 2008), during it (February 2008 to May 2009), and after it (June 2009 to December 2009).
Before the FDA warning period, a significant upward trend in AED prescription claims of 0.01% per month (99% CI: 0.008% to 0.013%, p<0.0001) was estimated.

Relative to the prewarning period, no significant change in trend was detected during the warning period (-20.0%, 99% CI: -70.0% to 30.0%, p=0.34) or after it (80.0%, 99% CI: -20.0% to 200.0%, p=0.03).

After stratification, no diagnostic group — epilepsy alone, epilepsy with comorbid psychiatric disorder, or psychiatric disorder alone — experienced a significant change in trend across the entire study period (p>0.01).

The retrieved evidence does not show that local anesthesia reduces pain during MR arthrography of the shoulder: in a patient survey of 74 patients undergoing arthrographic injection, mean VAS pain scores were 20.8 (median 10.5, SD 24.3) in the 36 patients who received local anesthetics versus 19.3 (median 13.0, SD 20.7) in the 38 who did not (P = 0.83, Mann-Whitney U test).

In the randomized MR arthrography study, 249 outpatients (178 men and 71 women; mean age, 44.4 years ± 14.6; range, 15-79) who underwent MRa were enrolled, and patients were randomly assigned into one of three groups, with group A (n=61) receiving skin infiltration with local anesthesia and control groups B (n=92) and C (n=96) receiving no local anesthesia.

In that randomized study, pain levels were assessed immediately after the injection for MRa using a horizontal visual analog scale (VAS) ranging from 0 to 10, and the three groups' pain scores for male and female patients were compared with a two-way analysis of variance.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Pain scores with versus without local anesthesia from the randomized three-group MR arthrography study.

In the TCD study, recanalization rates and poor 3-month outcomes (modified Rankin scale >2) of men and women were compared using the chi-square test, and multiple regression analysis was used to assess sex as a predictor of recanalization and poor 3-month outcome after controlling for age, baseline NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS), time to treatment, hypertension, and blood glucose.

369 patients had TCD examinations before or during IV rt-PA treatment; the 199 men (53.9%) and 170 women (46.1%) had mean ages of 67 ± 13 and 70 ± 14 years, respectively, and the sexes did not differ significantly in baseline stroke severity, time to TCD examination, or time to thrombolysis.

Of the men, 68 (34.2%) had complete recanalization, 58 (29.1%) had partial recanalization, and 73 (36.6%) had no recanalization, compared with women, of whom 53 (31.2%) had complete recanalization, 46 (27%) had partial recanalization, and 71 (41.8%) had no recanalization (p = 0.6).
Multiple regression analyses showed no difference between the sexes in recanalization rate, time to recanalization, or clinical outcome at 3 months.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: sex differences in 3-month outcome after IV tPA in the SITS-ISTR registry.

Yes — in a London-wide study of 93,375 cancer deaths among people aged 65 years and over who died between 2001 and 2010, country of birth used as a proxy for ethnicity was associated with where people died after adjustment, with deaths in hospital more likely for those born in Asia (proportion ratio (PR) 1.12, 95% CI 1.08-1.15, p<0.001) and Africa (PR 1.11, 95% CI 1.07-1.16, p<0.001).
In that cohort, most deaths (52.5%) occurred in hospital, followed by home (18.7%).

After adjustment, hospice deaths were less likely for decedents born in Asia (PR 0.73, 95% CI 0.68-0.80, p<0.001), Africa (PR 0.83, 95% CI 0.74-0.93, p<0.001) and 'other' geographical regions (PR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82-0.98, p<0.001), while home deaths were less likely for those born in the Caribbean (PR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85-0.98, p<0.001).

Over the study period, hospital deaths declined with an increase in home deaths, with annual trends of 0.50%/yr (95% CI 0.36-0.64) for those born in the UK, 1.00%/yr (0.64-1.30) for Europe, 1.09%/yr (0.94-1.20) for Asia and 1.03%/yr (0.72-1.30) for the Caribbean, all p<0.001, although time-consistent gaps across the geographical groups remained.

A limitation entailed by this design is that country of birth was used as a proxy for ethnicity, and the analyses report associations between country of birth and place of death rather than establishing that ethnicity causes differences in where people with cancer die.

Diffusion-weighted imaging was not a statistically significant indicator of the development of vascularization in hypovascular hepatocellular lesions: in a retrospective evaluation of 42 hypovascular hepatocellular lesions diagnosed by CT arteriography, the 730-day cumulative developments of vascularization were 17% for hypointense, 30% for isointense and 40% for hyperintense lesions, and the differences among these developments were not statistically significant.

In that study the lesion signal on DWI was classified as isointense, hypointense, or hyperintense, and follow-up studies that included intravenous dynamic CT or magnetic resonance imaging were performed.

No: in a retrospective cohort of 151 women with bothersome mixed urinary incontinence, concomitant anterior/apical (AA) repair added to a midurethral sling (MUS) did not improve the overactive bladder component, with a 6-week OAB-q Symptom Severity (OAB-q SS) change score of 30 ± 26 for MUS-only versus 25 ± 25 for MUS + AA (p = 0.20), indicating similar improvements in OAB symptoms in both groups.
Of the 151 women in the cohort, 67 (44%) underwent MUS-only and 84 (56%) underwent MUS + AA; the MUS-only group was younger and had less severe baseline prolapse (p < 0.05 for both).

Multivariate linear regression analysis also revealed no difference in OAB-q SS change score between the MUS-only and MUS + AA cohorts, although change scores were lower among women who had a postoperative complication (β = -19, 95% CI -31 to -6; p < 0.01).

Across all subjects, mean OAB-q SS scores improved significantly after surgery (p < 0.05), so the improvement in overactive bladder symptoms was attributable to surgery overall rather than to the addition of anterior/apical repair.

In the same study, which measured pubertal status and recent (30-day) alcohol use, the two-level (individuals nested within schools) logistic regression model, with main effects entered first and interaction terms added second, found significant main effects for pubertal stage: boys in middle puberty had increased odds of alcohol use, and girls in advanced puberty had increased odds of alcohol use.

No, parents did not have a moderating role: in a cross-sectional survey of 7631 adolescents aged 10–14 from 231 Australian schools, the interaction of family factors (parent-adolescent emotional closeness, family conflict, and parental permissiveness of alcohol use) and pubertal stage did not improve the fit of the model, so a main effect model of family factors and pubertal stage was adopted.

HIF1A is characterized in the study as a major vascular epithelial growth factor regulator under hypoxic conditions, and the study enrolled 87 AMD patients and 80 healthy subjects at the Department of Ophthalmology, Pamukkale University Hospital, Denizli, Turkey, of whom 45 (52%) had wet-type AMD and 42 (48%) had dry-type AMD.

In that case-control analysis, both rs11549465 and rs11549467 (HIF1A) were investigated in DNA isolated from peripheral blood samples of cases and controls by dye-termination DNA sequencing, and no statistically significant difference in the distributions of the HIF1A single nucleotide polymorphisms emerged between patients and healthy subjects; the only significant genetic association reported in this cohort was for CFH rs1061170, where having at least one C allele increased AMD risk independent of age (OR = 2.42, 95% CI 1.22-4.81).

The retrieved evidence does not report an overall proportion of pediatric concussion patients who were compliant with all discharge instructions; it reports selected adherence-related measures (physician and trainer follow-up, return to activity, symptoms, and medical clearance) from a single prospective cohort study of 150 patients.

That prospective cohort was conducted from November 2011 to November 2012 in a pediatric emergency department at a regional Level 1 trauma center serving 35,000 pediatric patients per year, and enrolled 150 patients aged 8 to 17 years who were discharged from the ED with a diagnosis of concussion; adherence was assessed by telephone follow-up surveys at 2 weeks and 4 weeks after the ED visit.
Physician follow-up was equivalent for sport and nonsport concussions (2 weeks, 58%; 4 weeks, 64%).
Sports-related concussion patients were more likely to follow up with a trainer (2 weeks, 25% vs.
Of the patients who did return to play or normal activities at 2 weeks (44%), more than one third (35%) were symptomatic, and most (58%) did not receive medical clearance.
Of the patients who had returned to activities at 4 weeks (64%), less than one quarter (23%) were symptomatic, and most (54%) received medical clearance.

Because these findings come from a prospective cohort that measured self-reported follow-up and activity status at 2 and 4 weeks, they describe the frequency of those specific behaviors rather than a composite measure of compliance with the full set of discharge instructions.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: overall proportion of pediatric concussion patients compliant with all discharge instructions.

Using Manitoba administrative data, Francophones living outside urban areas had lower rates of diagnosed substance use disorder (rate ratio 0.80; 95% CI 0.68 to 0.95) and of suicide and suicide attempts (rate ratio 0.59; 95% CI 0.43 to 0.79) than non-Francophones, while across the province no differences were found between the two groups in rates of diagnosed mood disorders, anxiety disorders, dementia, or any mental disorders after adjusting for age, sex, and geographic area.
In representative survey samples, Francophones were less likely than non-Francophones to report that their mental health was excellent, very good, or good (66.9% versus 74.2%).

Joint line (JL) positions were assessed from the contralateral knee in a study that used scaled weight-bearing anteroposterior radiographs of both knees, in which two independent observers measured the distances from the fibular head, the medial and lateral epicondyle, and the adductor tubercle to the JL, in 200 knees of 100 patients (50 men and 50 women).
For the fibular head, the mean difference between the treated and the control knee was 0.0 mm, with narrow confidence limits ranging from -1.1 to 1.1.

Reconstructing the natural joint line in knee revision surgery improves clinical and functional outcome but may be challenging when both cartilage and bone were removed during previous operations, and because of the inherent symmetry of the human body the authors hypothesised that JLs may be directly assessed by measuring the distances from bony landmarks to the JL of the contralateral knee on radiographic images.

The retrieved study reports radiographic distance measurements between bony landmarks and the contralateral joint line and does not report clinical or planning outcomes of knee revision surgery, so it cannot establish that contralateral-knee joint line assessment improves or guides planning of knee revision surgery.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: comparison results for the medial epicondyle, lateral epicondyle, and adductor tubercle distances between the treated and control knees.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: evidence that contralateral-knee joint line assessment improves or guides planning of knee revision surgery.

Yes, in a retrospective case-control study, anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) failure was associated with steeper medial and lateral posterior tibial slopes (PTS): the odds ratio of ACLR failure was 6.8 for medial PTS >= 5 degrees (P = 0.007) and 10.8 for lateral PTS >= 5 degrees (P = 0.000).

The study comprised 20 ACLR failure cases and 20 randomly selected controls, drawn from 238 eligible patients identified between June 2009 and October 2010, and reported an overall ACLR failure rate of 8.4%.

The medial PTS of the ACLR failure group was reported as significantly steeper than that of the control group, with values of 3.5 degrees +/- 2.5 degrees versus 6.1 degrees +/- 2.1 degrees (P = 0.000).
The lateral PTS of the ACLR failure group was likewise reported as significantly steeper than that of the control group, at 2.9 degrees +/- 2.1 degrees versus 5.5 degrees +/- 3.0 degrees (P = 0.006).

Medial and lateral PTS were measured on magnetic resonance imaging scans using Hudek's measurement method; across all 40 participants the mean medial PTS was 4.1 degrees +/- 3.2 degrees and the mean lateral PTS was 4.6 degrees +/- 2.6 degrees.

Because these findings come from a retrospective case-control comparison of PTS between failure and control groups, the design supports an association between steeper PTS and ACLR failure but cannot establish that modifying or lowering PTS prevents graft failure.

Parents of overweight children showed limited recall of the feedback they received after BMI screening: overall 39% of the information was recalled, a mean score of 6.3 out of a possible 16, while 94% of parents were able to correctly recall their child's weight status.

In a randomised controlled trial of different feedback methods, 1093 children aged 4-8 years were screened, but only overweight children (n=271, 24.7%) were included; their parents were randomised to receive feedback via best practice care (BPC) or motivational interviewing (MI) at face-to-face interviews typically lasting 20-40 minutes, and 244 (90%) parents took part in a follow-up interview 2 weeks later to assess recall and understanding of the feedback session information.
Parents given feedback via BPC recalled more than those in the MI group (difference in total score 0.48; 95% CI 0.05 to 0.92).

Maternal education (0.81; 0.25 to 1.37) and parental ratings of how useful they found the information (0.19; 0.04 to 0.35) were significant predictors of recall score in multivariate analyses, with recall measured from audio-taped, verbatim-transcribed interviews coded for amount and accuracy.
Understanding of the weight information was poor: although 94% of parents correctly recalled their child's weight status, fewer than 10 parents could accurately describe what the measurements meant.

Because the trial's randomised comparison and 2-week follow-up interview assessed recall and understanding of the feedback session rather than downstream outcomes, it does not establish that either feedback method changed children's weight or behaviour.

Sternal fractures in childhood are rare: a total of 4 children aged 5-14 years with a sternal fracture were treated in 2 years, of whom 2 were hospitalized for pain management and 2 remained in outpatient care; cases were recorded from January 2010 to December 2012 among all inpatients and outpatients according to the documentation.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Frequency of missed or overlooked sternal fractures in growing children.

Yes — clinical pathologists report red blood cell morphologic (RBC-M) changes to help clinicians prioritize differential diagnoses, but this reporting is subjective, semiquantitative and potentially biased, and a survey of 1662 clinicians and 82 clinical pathologists found that clinicians do not always interpret such reports as intended.
In that online survey of analyzable responses from 1662 clinicians and 82 clinical pathologists, a quiz assessed respondent groups' understanding of RBC-M terms.
All respondent groups interpreted certain terms correctly, for example Heinz bodies, whereas some clinicians misinterpreted other terms, for example eccentrocytes.
Clinical pathologists often do not report RBC-M changes they consider insignificant when these are present in low numbers.

The cited survey evidence indicates discordance between clinical pathologists and clinicians: reporting decisions vary among clinical pathologists, and reports may not be interpreted by clinicians as intended.
Both clinicians and clinical pathologists considered some terms, for example agglutination, useful, whereas only clinical pathologists considered other terms, for example ghost cells, useful.
Twenty-eight percent of clinicians thought clinical pathologists review all blood smears, while only 19% of clinical pathologists reported reviewing all smears.
The survey's discordance is reflected in term interpretation, since all groups interpreted some terms such as Heinz bodies correctly while some clinicians misinterpreted others such as eccentrocytes.

The study was a cross-sectional survey of 27,375 white respondents to the Canadian Community Health Survey (CCHS) Healthy Aging 2008/2009, and its objective was to examine whether government-funded, low-income vision care programs improve use of eye care services by low-income individuals in Canada.

Government-funded, low-income vision care programs were reviewed, and the amount of assistance provided was compared with professional fee schedules for general/routine eye examinations and market prices for eyeglasses.
In 5 provinces, low-income vision care assistance fully covers a general/routine eye examination; in the remainder, the assistance provided is insufficient for a general/routine eye examination.
Assistance for eyeglasses is inadequate in 5 provinces, requiring out-of-pocket copayments.
To receive low-income vision care assistance, individuals must be in receipt of social assistance, and the criteria for receiving social assistance are stringent.
The Canadian Financial Capability Survey revealed that 7.9% of Canadians aged 45 to 64 years and 5.5% aged 65 years or older received social assistance in 2009.
The CCHS found in 2008/2009 that 12.5% of citizens aged 45 to 64 years and 13.2% of those aged 65 years or older had difficulty paying for basic expenses such as food.

Among middle-aged whites who self-reported not having glaucoma, cataracts, diabetes, or vision problems not corrected by lenses, utilization of eye care providers was 28.1% among those with financial difficulty versus 41.9% among those without (p<0.05), giving a prevalence ratio of 0.68 (95% CI 0.57-0.80) adjusted for age, sex and education.

The retrieved evidence does not establish whether government-funded vision care assistance increases eye care utilization among low-income individuals compared with no assistance; the utilization result reported is a cross-sectional association between self-reported financial difficulty and eye care provider use, not an assistance-versus-no-assistance evaluation.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: government-funded vision care assistance increases eye care utilization among low-income individuals compared with no assistance.

In a prospective pilot study of 23 consecutive patients (12 male, 11 female) with a stage III or stages III and IV osteochondritis dissecans lesion (mostly stage III) who were admitted for surgery, a distinct serum vitamin D3 deficiency was found in the majority (18/23), two patients were vitamin D3-insufficient, and in three patients the vitamin D3 level reached the lowest normal value.

The aim of this prospective pilot study was to analyse whether vitamin D insufficiency or deficiency might be a contributing etiological factor in the development of an OCD lesion; however, because the study was a single-arm pilot without a control group and without pre-lesion or longitudinal vitamin D measurements, the reported finding of low vitamin D3 levels in affected patients does not establish a causal or temporal relationship between vitamin D insufficiency/deficiency and the development of osteochondritis dissecans.

The retrieved evidence does not establish: a demonstrated causal or temporal relationship between vitamin D insufficiency/deficiency and the development of OCD (no control group, no pre-lesion or longitudinal vitamin D data).

The cited evidence is insufficient to establish that the inverse equity hypothesis applies over time to cancer screening coverage in middle-income countries: the only retrieved study is a secondary analysis of cross-sectional WHO Study on Global Ageing and Adult Health data from China, Mexico, Russia and South Africa (2007-2010), which can show whether inequalities are lower where aggregate coverage is higher but cannot show whether inequalities narrow as coverage increases over time.
In that cross-sectional analysis, economic inequalities in screening participation were substantially lower or non-existent in countries with higher aggregate coverage.

Reported coverage was 10.5% for breast cancer screening in South Africa, 19.3% in China, 33.8% in Russia and 43% in Mexico, and 24% for cervical cancer screening in South Africa, 27.2% in China, 63.7% in Mexico and 81.5% in Russia.

Relative Index of Inequality values for breast cancer screening were 14.57 in South Africa, 4.90 in China, 2.01 in Mexico and 1.04 in Russia, and for cervical cancer screening 3.60 in China, 2.47 in South Africa, 1.39 in Mexico and 1.12 in Russia.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Temporal narrowing of economic inequalities in cancer screening participation as coverage increases over time.

In the cited regional cohort, early surfactant administration (within one hour of birth) versus late administration had little or no impact on chronic lung disease (CLD) or mortality before/at 36 weeks once multivariable analysis was applied, although the crude rates of CLD and mortality were higher in the early group (40.2% versus 20.0%) because that group was less mature (27.1 ± 2.1 versus 29.4 ± 2.1 weeks).

The comparison was made in a geographically defined population of premature infants born at 22-32 weeks' gestation between January 2006 and December 2009, using a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from the regional NICU database covering ten neonatal intensive care units in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory, Australia; the primary outcome was CLD and mortality before/at 36 weeks.
Of the 2170 infants who received surfactant, 1182 (54.5%) received early surfactant and 988 (45.5%) received late surfactant.
In multivariable analysis, early surfactant was associated with less duration of ventilation, longer duration of CPAP and longer hospital stay, but with little or no impact on CLD/mortality.

Because the analysis was a retrospective review of observational cohort data, the higher crude CLD and mortality rate in the early surfactant group cannot by itself establish that the timing of surfactant administration caused the difference in CLD or mortality, as the groups differed markedly in gestational age.
For women, the correlation between circulating androgens and sexual desire is inconclusive, based on a cross-sectional study of 560 healthy women aged 19-65 years.

In that cross-sectional study of 560 healthy women aged 19-65 years divided into three age groups, sexual desire was determined as the total score of the sexual desire domain of the Female Sexual Function Index, and total testosterone (TT), calculated free testosterone (FT), androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS), and the androgen metabolite ADT-G were analyzed using mass spectrometry, with correlations considered statistically significant at P<0.05.
Sexual desire correlated overall with FT and androstenedione in the total cohort of women.

In a subgroup of women aged 25-44 years with no use of systemic hormonal contraception, sexual desire correlated with TT, FT, androstenedione, and DHEAS, whereas in women aged 45-65 years only androstenedione correlated with sexual desire.
No correlations between ADT-G and sexual desire were identified.
Because the reported design was cross-sectional, the observed associations between androgen measures and sexual desire cannot establish that altering androgen levels changes sexual desire in women.

The retrieved evidence does not establish that participant information sheet content and presentation influence recruitment or participation for an antenatal intervention; the single study instead assessed pregnant women's and trainee midwives' perceptions of an antenatal intervention.

The study aimed to assess the extent to which the title and font of participant information sheets (PISs) can influence pregnant women's and trainee midwives' perceptions of an antenatal intervention.

Pregnant women (n=35) and trainee midwives (n=36) were randomly presented with one of four PISs in which title and font were manipulated to create four experimental conditions: Double Fluent; Double Awkward; Fluent Title–Awkward Font; and Awkward Title–Fluent Font.
After reading the PIS, participants rated their perceptions of the intervention on Attractiveness, Complexity, Expected Risk and Required Effort using five-point Likert scales.

A 4×2 factorial multivariate analysis of variance showed that pregnant women rated the Double Awkward condition as significantly more complex than the Double Fluent condition (p=.024) and the Awkward Title–Fluent Font condition (p=.021).
The retrieved evidence does not establish: recruitment and participation for an antenatal intervention.

Yes — in a population-based cohort of 1,100 randomly sampled Saskatchewan adults, neck pain was associated with worse physical health-related quality of life (HRQoL) 6 months later, but no association was found between neck pain and mental HRQoL.

The SF-36 questionnaire was used to measure physical and mental HRQoL 6 months later, and the study found an exposure-response relationship between neck pain and physical HRQoL after adjusting for age, education, arthritis, low back pain, and depressive symptomatology.

Compared with participants without neck pain at baseline, those with mild (β=-1.53, 95% CI -2.83, -0.24), intense (β=-3.60, 95% CI -5.76, -1.44), or disabling (β=-8.55, 95% CI -11.68, -5.42) neck pain had worse physical HRQoL 6 months later.
No association was found between neck pain and mental HRQoL.

Among the four 6-month neck pain trajectories (no or mild, improving, worsening, and persistent neck pain), a worsening course of neck pain and persistent neck pain were associated with worse physical HRQoL.

Because the earlier evidence linking neck pain to HRQoL was cross-sectional, it could not inform the association between neck pain and future HRQoL; the cited cohort study was designed to address HRQoL 6 months later.

In a retrospective review of 113 adult patients with obstructive sleep apnea who underwent upper airway surgery (nasal or uvulopalatopharyngoplasty [UPPP]) at a Beijing academic hospital in 2012-2013 and had preoperative and postoperative serum lipid profiles, surgery was associated with significant reductions in serum total cholesterol (TC, 4.86±0.74 to 4.69±0.71) and lipoprotein(a) (LP(a), median 18.50 to 10.90) post-operatively (P<0.01 and P=0.01, respectively), with no significant change in serum HDL, LDL or triglycerides (P>0.05 for all).

By procedure type, among the 51 UPPP patients serum TC, HDL and LP(a) improved (P=0.01, P=0.01 and P<0.01, respectively), whereas among the 62 nasal-surgery patients only serum LP(a) decreased (P<0.01).

Results differed by baseline lipid status: in patients with normal serum lipids at baseline only serum LP(a) decreased (P<0.01); in patients with isolated hypertriglyceridemia serum HDL, triglycerides and LP(a) showed significant improvements (P=0.02, P=0.03 and P<0.01, respectively); in patients with isolated hypercholesterolemia serum LP(a) decreased significantly (P=0.01) with a similar trend for serum TC (P=0.06); and in patients with mixed hyperlipidemia serum TC and LDL also decreased (P=0.02 and P=0.03, respectively).

Because the evidence comes from a retrospective review of 113 adult patients who underwent surgery, the reported postoperative lipid changes are associations within a single-arm before-after series and cannot by themselves establish that airway surgery causally lowers serum lipids in obstructive sleep apnea patients.

Yes, a tendency to clear one's plate when eating may be a risk factor for obesity in an environment where food is plentiful, based on a positive association between plate clearing and body weight in a US sample.

Among 993 US adults (60% male, 80% American European, mean age 31 years) who completed self-report measures of habitual plate clearing plus behavioral and demographic characteristics, plate clearing tendencies were positively associated with BMI (β=0.18, 95% CI 0.07-0.29, P<0.001), and this association remained after accounting for a large number of other demographic and behavioral predictors of BMI; an increased tendency to plate clear was associated with a significantly higher body weight.
The reported finding is an association derived from self-report measures of habitual plate clearing and body weight, so it does not by itself establish that plate clearing causes weight gain.

The purposes of this study were to report the alveolar process thickness and inter-radicular space in the posterior region of the mandible, to assess the impact of different miniscrew insertion angle protocols, and to identify differences between the genders or types of malocclusion.
The primary outcome variables were bone thickness and inter-radicular space.

The inter-radicular spaces were evaluated 5 mm from the cement-enamel junction, and the bone thicknesses were taken at 45°, 60°, and 90° in relation to the alveolar ridge, simulating a miniscrew insertion.
In this retrospective study, 100 individuals were selected for orthodontic treatment at a radiology clinic; cone-beam computed tomography data were imported into 3-dimensional software.
The sample was composed of 100 patients with a mean age of 17.4 ± 6.74 years; there were 61 female and 39 male patients and 60 Class I and 40 Class II molar relationships.
The inter-radicular space ranged from 2.46 to 3.31 mm, and alveolar bone thickness ranged from 8.01 to 13.77 mm.
The thickness tended to decrease with the increase in insertion angle from 45° to 90°, and no significant differences between the genders or types of malocclusion were found.
To compare the inter-radicular space and the thickness of bone between areas, an analysis of variance for repeated measures was used.

The retrieved evidence reports alveolar process thickness, inter-radicular space, and simulated insertion angles but does not report miniscrew placement success or failure outcomes; therefore it does not establish that bone thickness or inter-radicular space affect miniscrew placement in posterior mandibular sites.

The study was a retrospective analysis of cone-beam computed tomography measurements; such observational data can describe dimensional relationships and variation with simulated insertion angle, but they do not establish that changing bone thickness or inter-radicular space would alter miniscrew placement outcomes.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: actual effect of bone thickness and inter-radicular space on miniscrew placement outcomes in posterior mandibular sites.

Elderly patients largely do not report intending to call 911 when presented with clinical scenarios suggestive of acute stroke: in a cross-sectional study of 367 out-patients aged 60 years or older in Buenos Aires, Argentina, only 14% correctly endorsed intention to call 911 on the Stroke Action Test, against a pre-set cut-off of at least 75% for correct endorsement.

When presented with the most typical stroke signs and symptoms, only 65% of these elderly adults reported that they would call an ambulance; amaurosis fugax was the symptom for which an ambulance was reported to be called the least (15%), and on average the correct response was chosen only 37% of the time.

Because this was a cross-sectional study that used a standardized questionnaire to assess correct endorsement of the intention to call 911 among elderly out-patients, the reported percentages describe self-reported intention rather than observed calls actually made for real stroke events.

The cited evidence is insufficient to establish that transcranial direct current stimulation can differentiate unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS) from minimally conscious state (MCS): the single retrieved study applied anodal tDCS over the orbitofrontal cortex to boost or unmask cortical connectivity and excitability, not to test diagnostic discrimination between the two clinical groups.

In that study, baseline electrophysiological evaluation showed, relative to healthy controls, a partial preservation of cortical effective connectivity and excitability in clinically defined MCS, whereas these components were absent in clinically defined UWS.
After the anodal tDCS protocol over the orbitofrontal cortex, cortical connectivity and excitability were boosted in all healthy controls and MCS patients and were unmasked in some UWS patients.
The study enrolled 25 severe disorders of consciousness patients, following post-anoxic or traumatic brain injury, and 20 healthy individuals as a control group.
The retrieved evidence does not establish: Evidence that tDCS can differentiate UWS from MCS.

In preoperative locoregional T staging of gastric cancer, EUS showed higher sensitivity (94%) than MDCT and MRI (65% and 76%; p = 0.02 and p = 0.08), while MDCT and MRI had significantly higher specificity (91% and 89%) than EUS (60%) (p = 0.0009 and p = 0.003).

For N staging, EUS showed higher sensitivity (92%) than MRI and MDCT (69% and 73%; p = 0.01 and p = 0.02), and MDCT showed better specificity (81%) than EUS and MRI (58% and 73%; p = 0.03 and p = 0.15).
Adding MRI to MDCT or EUS did not result in significant differences for sensitivity in the preoperative locoregional staging of gastric cancer.

In a prospective comparison of 52 patients with biopsy-proven gastric cancer who underwent preoperative 1.5-T MRI, 64-channel MDCT and EUS, with all images analysed blind against histopathological findings according to the seventh edition of the TNM classification, MRI gave higher T-staging specificity (89%) than EUS (60%; p = 0.003) but lower T-staging sensitivity (76%) than EUS (94%; p = 0.08), and for N staging MRI was less sensitive (69%) than EUS (92%; p = 0.01) and less specific (73%) than MDCT (81%; p = 0.15), so its added sensitivity to MDCT or EUS was not significant.

In a series of 158 gastric cancer samples from patients who underwent gastrectomy between 2002 and 2008, immunohistochemical loss of DKK3 protein expression was found in 64 of 158 (40.5%) samples, and this loss was associated with advanced T stage (p<0.001), lymph node metastasis (p<0.001), UICC TNM stage (p<0.001), tumor location (p=0.029), lymphovascular invasion (p=0.035) and perineural invasion (p=0.032).

Yes, the study reports preoperative predictive value: loss of DKK3 expression was associated with lymph node metastasis (p<0.001), and the combination of DKK3 expression status with computed tomography (CT) increased the accuracy of CT staging for predicting lymph node involvement from 71.5% to 80.0% in patients with advanced gastric cancer (AGC).

The reported nodal-prediction gain is based on DKK3 expression measured by immunohistochemistry in gastrectomy specimens from a retrospective series, so the association between DKK3 loss and lymph node metastasis is not by itself evidence that a preoperative DKK3 measurement predicts nodal status; the 71.5% to 80.0% accuracy figures apply to DKK3 status combined with preoperative CT-based clinical staging in AGC patients.
To test the predictive value of distal ureteral diameter (UD) on reflux resolution after endoscopic injection in children with primary vesicoureteral reflux (VUR).

This was a retrospective review of patients diagnosed with primary VUR between 2009 and 2012 who were managed by endoscopic injection; seventy patients were enrolled in this series (17 boys and 53 girls), and mean age was 5.9 years (1.2-13 years).
Clinical outcome was defined as reflux resolution.
Macroplastique injection was performed in all; grade III presented in 37 patients (53%), and 33 patients (47%) were of grade IV.
Mean distal UD was 5.5 mm (2.5-13 mm) and mean UDR was 37.8% (18%-70%).
The effect of grade, UD, and UDR on success after endoscopic injection was tested.
UD and UDR were significant predictors of reflux resolution on logistic regression analysis (P <.007 and.001, respectively).

As a retrospective review, the reported association between distal ureteral diameter measures and reflux resolution does not establish that intervening on these measurements changes the likelihood of reflux resolution.

Yes — in the longitudinal study of 500 men (250 sons of men with a lifetime history of substance use disorder, the High Average Risk group, and 250 sons of men with no such history, the Low Average Risk group), the Transmissible Liability Index measured at ages 10-12 in late childhood was significantly associated with the number and severity of lifetime suicide attempts.

The Transmissible Liability Index was delineated at baseline (age 10-12) and age-specific versions were administered at 12-14, 16, 19, 22, and 25 years of age, covering suicidal behavior from preadolescence (12-14) through young adulthood (25).
